Now the king of Aram had commanded the commanders of the chariotry that {was} to him, saying, “You shall not fight small, great, but with the king of Israel alone.”

And it happened, when the commanders of the chariotry saw Jehoshaphat, that they, they said, “He {is} the king of Israel!” And they turned aside to fight against him. And Jehoshaphat cried out, and Yahweh helped him, and God incited them from him.
And it happened, when the commanders of the chariotry saw that he was not the king of Israel, that they turned back from after him.

But a man drew the bow in his innocence, and he struck the king of Israel between the joints and between the armor. And he said to his charioteer, “Turn your hand and bring me out from the camp, for I am wounded.”
And the battle went up on that day, and the king of Israel was propped up in the chariot opposite Aram until the evening. And he died at the time of the going in of the sun.
And Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, returned to his house in peace, to Jerusalem.

But Jehu, the son of Hanani, the seer, came out to his face, and he said to King Jehoshaphat, “Should you help the wicked and love the haters of Yahweh? And because of this, wrath {is} upon you from the face of Yahweh.
Nevertheless, good things have been found with you, for you have consumed the Asherahs from the land, and you have established your heart to seek God.”
And Jehoshaphat dwelled in Jerusalem. And he returned and went out among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim. And he made them return to Yahweh, the God of their fathers.
And he appointed judges in the land in all of the fortified cities of Judah, for city and city.
And he said to the judges, “See what you are doing. For you do not judge for man but for Yahweh; and with you in a matter of judgment.
And now, let the fear of Yahweh be upon you. Watch and act, for with Yahweh our God there is no iniquity or lifting of faces or taking of a bribe.”
And also in Jerusalem Jehoshaphat appointed from the Levites and the priests and from the heads of fathers for Israel for the judgment of Yahweh and for dispute. (For they had returned to Jerusalem.)
And he commanded them, saying, “Thus you shall do in the fear of Yahweh, in trustworthiness and with a whole heart.

And any dispute that comes to you from your brothers, the ones dwelling in their cities, between blood to blood, between law to command, to statutes and to judgments, then you shall warn them, and they will not become guilty toward Yahweh and wrath will {not} be on you and on your brothers. Thus you shall do, and you will not be guilty.

And behold, Amariah the head priest {is} over you for any matter of Yahweh, and Zebadiah, the son of Ishmael, the leader of the house of Judah, for any matter of the king. And the Levites {are} officers to your faces. Be strong and act, and may Yahweh be with the good!”
And it happened after this, the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, and with them from the Ammonites, came against Jehoshaphat for battle.
And they came and declared to Jehoshaphat, saying, “A great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea, from Aram. And behold them in Hazezon Tamar (it {is} Engedi).
And he feared, and Jehoshaphat set his face to seek Yahweh. And he proclaimed a fast over all of Judah.
And Judah gathered to seek from Yahweh. Even from all of the cities of Judah, they came to seek Yahweh.
And Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of Yahweh, to the face of the new courtyard.

And he said, “Yahweh, the God of our fathers, {are} you not he, the God in the heavens? And you are ruling over all of the kingdoms of the nations, and in your hand {are} power and might, and none stations himself with you.
You, our God, did you not dispossess the dwellers of this land from the face of your people Israel and give it to the seed of Abraham your friend, to eternity?
And they have dwelled in it, and they have built for you in it a sanctuary for your name, saying,

‘If harm comes upon us—the sword, judgment or pestilence or famine—we will stand to the face of this house and to your face, for your name {is} in this house, and we will cry out to you from our trouble, and may you hear, and may you save.’

And now, behold, the sons of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom you did not give to Israel to enter against them when they came from the land of Egypt, for they turned from against them, and they did not destroy them,
but behold them, repaying against us, coming to drive us out from your possession that you made us possess.
Our God, will you not judge them? For there is not strength in us to the face of this great multitude coming against us. And we, we do not know what we should do, but our eyes {are} upon you.”
And all of Judah was standing to the face of Yahweh, even their children, their wives, and their sons.
And Jahaziel, the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite from the sons of Asaph, the Spirit of Yahweh was upon him in the midst of the assembly.

And he said, “Attend, all of Judah and dwellers of Jerusalem and King Jehoshaphat. Thus says Yahweh to you, ‘You, may you not fear and may you not be dismayed from the face of this great multitude, for the battle {is} not to you but to God.
Tomorrow, go down against them. Behold them, coming up by the Ascent of Ziz. And you will find them at the end of the wadi, {to} the face of the wilderness of Jeruel.

{It is} not to you to fight in this. Station yourselves, stand and see the salvation of Yahweh with you, Judah and Jerusalem. May you not fear and may you not be dismayed. Tomorrow, go out to their face, and Yahweh {will be} with you.’”
And Jehoshaphat bowed down, nostrils earthward. And all of Judah and the dwellers of Jerusalem fell to the face of Yahweh to prostrate themselves to Yahweh.
And Levites from the sons of the Kohathites and from the sons of the Korahites arose to praise Yahweh, the God of Israel, with a great voice to upward.

And they got up early in the morning, and they went out to the wilderness of Tekoa. And when they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, “Hear me, Judah and dwellers of Jerusalem! Believe in Yahweh your God, and you will be confirmed. Believe in his prophets, and you will succeed.”

And he consulted with the people, and he stationed the singers to Yahweh and the praisers of the beauty of holiness in going out to the face of the equipped. And they were saying, “Thank Yahweh, for his covenant faithfulness {is} to eternity.”
And at the time they began with a joyful shout and praise, Yahweh put ambushes against the sons of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir coming to Judah, and they were struck.

For the sons of Ammon and Moab stood against the dwellers of Mount Seir, to devote and to destroy {them}. And when they finished with the dwellers of Seir, they helped, a man against his neighbor, for destruction.
And Judah came to the watchtower in the wilderness, and they turned toward the multitude, and behold, corpses fallen earthward! And there was no escape.

And Jehoshaphat and his people came to plunder their spoil, and they found among them in abundance both property and corpses and vessels of delight. And they delivered for themselves to no carrying away. And they were three days plundering the spoil, for it {was} great.
And on the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beracah. For they blessed Yahweh there, therefore they called the name of that place the Valley of Beracah, to today.
And they returned, every man of Judah and Jerusalem, and Jehoshaphat {was} at their head, to return to Jerusalem with rejoicing, for Yahweh had made them rejoice over their enemies.
And they came to Jerusalem with lyres and with harps and with trumpets to the house of Yahweh.
And the fear of God {was} upon all of the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that Yahweh had fought with the enemies of Israel.
And the kingdom of Jehoshaphat rested, for his God gave rest to him from around.
And Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. {He was} a son of 35 years when he reigned, and he reigned 25 years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother {was} Azubah, the daughter of Shilhi.
And he walked in the way of Asa his father, and he did not turn from it, doing right in the eyes of Yahweh.
However, they did not remove the high places. And the people still did not establish their heart to the God of their fathers.

Now the rest of the matters of Jehoshaphat, the first {ones} and the last {ones}, behold them, written in the words of Jehu, the son of Hanani, which is brought up on the scroll of the kings of Israel.
And after this, Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, allied himself with Ahaziah, the king of Israel. He, he acted wickedly by doing {this}.
And he allied himself with him to make ships to go {to} Tarshish. And they made the ships at Ezion Geber.

But Eliezer, the son of Dodavahu from Mareshah, prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, “When you allied yourself with Ahaziah, Yahweh broke through your works.” And the ships were broken, and they were not able to go to Tarshish.
And Jehoshaphat lay down with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in the City of David. And Jehoram his son reigned in his place.
Now brothers {were} to him, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah and Jehiel and Zechariah and Azariahu and Michael and Shephatiah. All of these {were} sons of Jehoshaphat, the king of Israel.
And their father gave to them many gifts of silver and of gold and of valuables, with cities of fortification in Judah. But the kingdom, he gave to Jehoram, for he {was} the firstborn.
And Jehoram arose over the kingdom of his father, and he strengthened himself. And he killed all of his brothers with the sword, and also some of the princes of Israel.
Jehoram {was} a son of 32 years when he reigned, and he reigned 8 years in Jerusalem.
And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab did, for a daughter of Ahab was a wife to him. And he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh.
But Yahweh was not willing to destroy the house of David because of the covenant that he had cut with David, and just as he had said, to give a lamp to him and to his sons all of the days.
In his days, Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah, and they made a king rule over them.
So Joram passed over with his commanders and all of the chariotry with him. And it happened, he arose at night, and he struck Edom having surrounded to him and the commanders of the chariotry.
So Edom has rebelled from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah rebelled at that time from under his hand, for he had abandoned Yahweh, the God of his fathers.
Also, he, he made high places in the hills of Judah, and he made the dwellers of Jerusalem whore, and he drove Judah away.

And a writing came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, “Thus says Yahweh, the God of David your father, ‘Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father and in the ways of Asa, the king of Judah,

but you have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and you have made Judah and the dwellers of Jerusalem whore like the whoring of the house of Ahab, and also, you have killed your brothers, the house of your father, the ones better than you,
behold Yahweh, striking a great striking among your people and among your sons and among your wives and among all of your property
and you with many sicknesses, with a disease of your intestines, until your intestines come out from the sickness, days upon days.’”
And Yahweh awakened against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabians who {were} at the hand of the Cushites,

and they came up against Judah, and they broke through it. And they carried away all of the property found in the house of the king, and also his sons and his wives, and a son was not left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.
And after all of this, Yahweh struck him in his intestines with a sickness to no cure.

And it happened to days from days, that at the time of the going out of the end of two years, his intestines came out because of his sickness, and he died with bad maladies. And his people did not make for him a burning like the burning of his fathers.
He was a son of 32 {years} when he reigned, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem, and he went with no desire. And they buried him in the City of David, but not in the graves of the kings.

And the dwellers of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, his youngest son, reign in his place, for the band having come with the Arabians into the camp had killed all of the older. And Ahaziah, the son of Jehoram, the king of Judah, reigned.
Ahaziah {was} a son of 42 years when he reigned, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother {was} Athaliah, the daughter of Omri.
He, he also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counselor to act wickedly.
And he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, like the house of Ahab, for they, they were counselors to him after the death of his father, for destruction to him.
He also walked in their counsel, and he went with Jehoram, the son of Ahab, the king of Israel, to war against Hazael, the king of Aram, at Ramoth Gilead. And the Arameans struck Joram.

And he returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the strikings that they had struck him at Ramah when he fought with Hazael, the king of Aram. And Ahaziah, the son of Jehoram, the king of Judah, went down to see Jehoram, the son of Ahab, in Jezreel because he was infirm.
And the destruction of Ahaziah was from God, to go to Joram. For when he came, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu, the son of Nimshi, whom Yahweh had anointed him to cut off the house of Ahab.
And it happened, when Jehu was judging with the house of Ahab, that he found the princes of Judah and the sons of the brothers of Ahaziah, ones ministering to Ahaziah, and he killed them.

And he sought Ahaziah; and they captured him (and he had been hiding himself in Samaria). And they brought him to Jehu, and they killed him. And they buried him, for they said, “He {is} the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought Yahweh with all of his heart.” And there was none to the house of Ahaziah to retain strength for the kingdom.
And Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son had died. And she arose, and she destroyed all of the seed of the kingdom of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath, a daughter of the king, took Joash, the son of Ahaziah, and she stole him away from the midst of the sons of the king being killed, and she put him and his nurse in the room of the beds. And Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest (for she was the sister of Ahaziah) hid him from the face of Athaliah, and she did not kill him.
And he was with them in the house of God, being hidden six years. And Athaliah was reigning over the land.

And in the seventh year, Jehoiada strengthened himself, and he took the commanders of hundreds, Azariah, the son of Jehoram, and Ishmael, the son of Jehohanan, and Azariah, the son of Obed, and Maaseiah, the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat, the son of Zichri, with him into a covenant.
And they went around in Judah, and they gathered the Levites from all of the cities of Judah and the heads of the fathers of Israel. And they came to Jerusalem.
And all of the assembly cut a covenant in the house of God with the king. And he said to them, “Behold, the son of the king will reign, just as Yahweh spoke about the sons of David.
This {is} the thing that you shall do. A third of you coming in on the Sabbath from the priests and from the Levites {shall be} keepers of the thresholds,
and a third {shall be} at the house of the king, and a third {shall be} at the Gate of the Foundation. And all of the people {shall be} in the courtyards of the house of Yahweh.

And let not one enter the house of Yahweh except the priests and the ministering ones of the Levites. They, they may enter, for they {are} holy. And all of the people shall keep the keeping of Yahweh.

And the Levites shall surround the king around, a man with his weapons in his hand, and one entering into the house shall be killed. And they will be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out.”

And the Levites and all of Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded. And they took, a man his men, the ones coming in on the Sabbath with the ones going out on the Sabbath, for Jehoiada the priest did not dismiss the divisions.
And Jehoiada the priest gave to the commanders of hundreds the spears and the shields and the large shields that {had been} to King David that {were in} the house of God.

And he stationed all of the people, and a man {had} his weapon in his hand, from the right shoulder of the house to the left shoulder of the house, to the altar and to the house, by the king all around.
And they brought out the son of the king, and they put a crown on him, and the testimony, and they made him reign, and Jehoiada and his sons anointed him. And they said, “May the king live!”
And Athaliah heard the sound of the people running and praising the king, and she came to the people {at} the house of Yahweh.

And she looked, and behold, the king was standing by the pillar at the entrance, and the commanders and the trumpeters {were} by the king, and all of the people of the land were rejoicing and blasting on trumpets, and the singers with instruments of song and teaching to praise. And Athaliah tore her clothes, and she said, “Conspiracy! Conspiracy!”

And Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds, the officers of the army, and he said to them, “Bring her out from the house to the ranks. And the one coming after her, let him be killed with the sword.” For the priest said, “May you not kill her {in} the house of Yahweh.”
And they put two hands to her, and she came to the entrance of the gate of horses {of} the house of the king, and they killed her there.
And Jehoiada cut a covenant between himself and between all of the people and between the king to become a people for Yahweh.
And all of the people entered the house of Baal, and they tore it down, and they shattered his altars and his images, and they killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, to the face of the altars.

And Jehoiada set the appointments of the house of Yahweh by the hand of the priests, the Levites whom David had assigned over the house of Yahweh, to offer the burnt offerings of Yahweh, as written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and with song by the hands of David.
And he stationed gatekeepers at the gates of the house of Yahweh, that the unclean should not enter in any way.

And he took the commanders of hundreds and the nobles and the rulers of the people and all of the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of Yahweh, and they entered in the midst of the Upper Gate {of} the house of the king. And they sat the king on the throne of the kingdom.
And all of the people of the land rejoiced, and the city rested, for they had killed Athaliah with the sword.
Joash {was} a son of seven years when he reigned. And he reigned 40 years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Zibiah, from Beersheba.
And Joash did right in the eyes of Yahweh all of the days of Jehoiada the priest.
And Jehoiada took up two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And it happened after this, it was with the heart of Joash to repair the house of Yahweh.

And he gathered the priests and the Levites, and he said to them, “Go out to the cities of Judah and gather from all of Israel enough silver to strengthen the house of your God year by year. And you, hasten to the matter.” But the Levites did not hasten.

And the king called for Jehoiada, the head, and he said to him, “Why have you not sought after the Levites to bring in from Judah and from Jerusalem the tribute of Moses the servant of Yahweh and the assembly of Israel for the tent of the testimony?”
For the wicked Athaliah, her sons had broken into the house of God, and they had also used all of the sacred {things} of the house of Yahweh for the Baals.
And the king spoke, and they made a chest, and they placed it by the gate of the house of Yahweh, outside.
And they gave voice in Judah and in Jerusalem to bring in to Yahweh the tribute of Moses the servant of God over Israel in the wilderness.
And all of the princes and all of the people rejoiced, and they brought in and they threw into the chest until to completion.

And it happened, at the time {when} one brought in the chest to the oversight of the king by the hand of the Levites, that when they saw that {there was} an abundance of silver, that a scribe of the king would come and an officer of the head priest. And they would empty the chest, and they would carry it and bring it back to its place. Thus they did to day by day, and they gathered silver to abundance.

And the king and Jehoiada gave it to the doers of the work of the service of the house of Yahweh. And they were hiring stonecutters and craftsmen to repair the house of Yahweh, and also for craftsmen of iron and bronze to strengthen the house of Yahweh.
And the doers of the work did, and the health of the work went up by their hand. And they made the house of God stand according to its measurement, and they strengthened it.

And when they finished, they brought the remainder of the silver to the face of the king and Jehoiada. And they made vessels for the house of Yahweh, items of ministry and burnt offerings and palms and vessels of gold and silver. And they were offering up burnt offerings at the house of Yahweh continually all of the days of Jehoiada.
And Jehoiada aged and became full {of} days, and he died, a son of 130 years at his death.
And they buried him in the City of David with the kings, for he had done good in Israel and with God and his house.
And after the death of Jehoiada, the princes of Judah came and prostrated themselves to the king. Then the king listened to them.
And they abandoned the house of Yahweh, the God of their fathers, and they served Asherahs and idols. And wrath was upon Judah and Jerusalem for this their guilt.
And he sent prophets among them to bring them back to Yahweh, and they testified against them, but they did not listen.

And the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah, the son of Jehoiada the priest. And he stood above the people, and he said to them, “Thus says God, ‘Why are you transgressing the commands of Yahweh, that you do not prosper? Because you have abandoned Yahweh, so he has abandoned you.”
But they conspired against him, and they stoned him {with} stone by the command of the king in the courtyard of the house of Yahweh.
And King Joash did not remember the covenant faithfulness that Jehoiada, his father, did with him, and he killed his son. And as he died, he said, “May Yahweh see and seek.”

And it happened at the turn of the year, the army of Aram came up against him, and they came to Judah and Jerusalem. And they destroyed all of the princes of the people from the people. And they sent all of the plunder to the king of Damascus.

Although the army of Aram came with a small amount of men, yet Yahweh gave a very large army into their hand because they had abandoned Yahweh, the God of their fathers. So they did judgment on Joash.

And when they went from him (for they had left him with many wounds), his servants conspired together against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest. And they killed him on his bed, and he died. And they buried him in the City of David, but they did not bury him in the graves of the kings.
And these {were} the ones having conspired together against him: Zabad, the son of Shimeath the Ammonitess, and Jehozabad, the son of Shimrith the Moabitess.

And his sons and the abundance of the burdens against him and the founding of the house of God, behold them, written in the treatise of the scroll of the kings. And Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
Amaziah {was} a son of 25 years {when} he reigned, and he reigned 29 years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother {was} Jehoaddan, from Jerusalem.
And he did right in the eyes of Yahweh, only not with a whole heart.
And it happened, when the kingdom was strong to him, that he struck his servants, the ones having struck the king, his father.

But he did not kill their sons, for as written in the law, in the scroll of Moses, what Yahweh commanded, saying, “Fathers shall not be killed for sons, and sons shall not be killed for fathers. Rather, a man shall be killed for his sin.”

And Amaziah gathered Judah, and he appointed them according to the house of the fathers, for commanders of thousands and for commanders of hundreds for all of Judah and Benjamin. And he mustered them from a son of 20 years and upward. And he found them, 300,000 chosen, going out to war grasping spear and large shield.
And he hired from Israel 100,000 warriors of valor for 100 kikkars of silver.
But a man of God came to him, saying, “O King, let not the army of Israel come with you, for Yahweh is not with Israel, all of the sons of Ephraim.
But you, come, act, be strong in battle. God will make you stumble to the face of the enemy, for there is power in God to help and to make stumble.”

And Amaziah said to the man of God, “And what to do about the 100 kikkars that I have given to the troop of Israel?” And the man of God said, “There is to Yahweh to give to you to multiply from this.”
And Amaziah separated them, the troop that had come to him from Ephraim, to go to their place. And their nose burned greatly against Judah, and they returned to their place in burning of nose.
And Amaziah strengthened himself, and he led forth his people. And he went to the Valley of Salt, and he struck the sons of Seir, 10,000.
And the sons of Judah captured 10,000 alive. And they brought them to the head of a cliff, and they threw them from the head of the cliff. And all of them were split open.

But the sons of the troop that Amaziah had sent back from going with him to battle, they raided against the cities of Judah from Samaria and to Beth Horon. And they struck 3,000 from them, and they plundered much plunder.

And it happened after Amaziah came from striking the Edomites that he brought the gods of the sons of Seir, and set them up for himself as gods. And he prostrated himself to the face of them, and he sacrificed to them.
And the nose of Yahweh burned against Amaziah. And he sent a prophet to him, and he said to him, “Why do you seek the gods of a people that did not deliver their people from your hand?”

And it happened, when he was speaking with him, that he said to him, “Have we made you a counselor to the king? Stop yourself! Why should they strike you?” And the prophet stopped. But he said, “I know that God has counseled to destroy you, because you have done this and you have not listened to my counsel.”
And Amaziah, the king of Judah, took counsel, and he sent to Joash, the son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu, the king of Israel, saying, “Come, let us see one another’s faces.”

And Joash, the king of Israel, sent to Amaziah, the king of Judah, saying, “A thornbush that was in Lebanon sent to a cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as a wife.’ But a beast of the field that was in Lebanon passed by, and it trampled the thornbush.
You have said, ‘Behold, you have struck Edom!’ And your heart has lifted you up to boast. Now stay in your house. Why should you contend with calamity, so that you will fall, you and Judah with you?”
But Amaziah did not listen, because it {was} from God, in order to give them into the hand because they sought the gods of Edom.
And Joash, the king of Israel, went up, and they saw one another’s faces, he and Amaziah, the king of Judah, at Beth Shemesh, which {is} to Judah.
And Judah was struck to the face of Israel. And they fled, a man to his tent.

And Joash, the king of Israel, captured Amaziah, the king of Judah, the son of Joash, the son of Ahaziah, at Beth Shemesh. And he brought him {to} Jerusalem, and he broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Gate of the Corner, 400 cubits.
And all of the gold and the silver and all of the vessels found in the house of God with Obed Edom and the treasuries of the house of the king and sons of pledges. And he returned {to} Samaria.
And Amaziah, the son of Joash, the king of Judah, lived after the death of Joash, the son of Jehoahaz, the king of Israel, 15 years.
Now the rest of the matters of Amaziah, the first {ones} and the last {ones}, do not behold them, written on the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel?
And from the time that Amaziah turned from after Yahweh, they conspired against him a conspiracy in Jerusalem. And he fled to Lachish. But they sent after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.
And they carried him on the horses, and they buried him with his fathers in the city of Judah.
And all of the people of Judah took Uzziah (now he {was} a son of 16 years), and they made him reign in place of his father Amaziah.
He, he built up Eloth, and he returned it to Judah after the king lay down with his fathers.
Uzziah {was} a son of 16 years when he reigned, and he reigned 52 years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother {was} Jekoliah, from Jerusalem.
And he did right in the eyes of Yahweh, like all that Amaziah his father had done.
And he was seeking God in the days of Zechariah, the one teaching in the seeing of God. And in the days of his seeking Yahweh, God made him prosper.
And he went out and fought with the Philistines, and he broke through the wall of Gath and the wall of Jabneh and the wall of Ashdod. And he built cities in Ashdod and among the Philistines.
And God helped him against the Philistines and against the Arabians dwelling in Gur Baal and the Meunites.

and I will not add to make the foot of Israel wander from upon the ground that I appointed to your fathers if only they will take care to do all that I have commanded them and all of the law and the statutes and the judgments by the hand of Moses.”
But Manasseh misled Judah and the dwellers of Jerusalem to do more evil than the nations that Yahweh had destroyed from the face of the sons of Israel.
And Yahweh spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they did not attend.
And Yahweh brought against them the commanders of the army that {was} to the king of Assyria. And they captured Manasseh with hooks, and they bound him in bronze, and they made him go into Babylon.
But when distress was to him, he entreated the face of Yahweh, his God, and he humbled himself greatly from to the face of the God of his fathers.
And he prayed to him; and he was entreated by him, and he heard his supplication, and he brought him back {to} Jerusalem, to his kingdom. And Manasseh knew that Yahweh, he {is} God.

And after this, he built an outer wall for the City of David, from the west to Gihon, in the wadi, and at the entrance of the Gate of Fish and around to Ophel, and he made it very high. And he put commanders of the army in all of the cities of fortification in Judah.

And he removed the gods of the foreigner and the idol from the house of Yahweh and all of the altars that he had built on the mountain of the house of Yahweh and in Jerusalem. And he threw {them} outside of the city.
And he established the altar of Yahweh, and he sacrificed on it sacrifices of peace offerings and a thank offering. And he said to Judah to serve Yahweh, the God of Israel.
Nevertheless, the people were still sacrificing on the high places, only to Yahweh their God.

Now the rest of the matters of Manasseh and his prayer to his God and the words of the seers, the ones speaking to him in the name of Yahweh, the God of Israel, behold them, on the matters of the kings of Israel.

And his prayer and his being entreated by him and all of his sin and his transgression and the places where he built high places on them and stationed Asherahs and idols to the face of his humbling himself, behold them, written in the words of Hozai.
And Manasseh lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in his house. And Amon his son reigned in his place.
Amon was a son of 22 years when he reigned, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
And he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, just as Manasseh his father had done. And to all of the idols that Manasseh his father had made, Amon sacrificed, and he served them.
And he did not humble himself from to the face of Yahweh, as Manasseh his father had humbled himself, but he, Amon, he multiplied guilt.
And his servants conspired against him, and they killed him in his house.
But the people of the land struck all of the ones having conspired against King Amon, and the people of the land made Josiah his son reign in his place.
Josiah was a son of 8 years when he reigned, and he reigned 31 years in Jerusalem.
And he did right in the eyes of Yahweh, and he walked in the ways of David his father, and he did not turn right or left.

And in eight years to his reigning, and he, he {was} still a youth, he began to seek the God of David, his father. And in year twelve, he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem from the high places and the Asherahs and the idols and the molded images.

And they tore down to his face the altars of the Baals, and the sun images that {were} to above from upon them, he cut down. And he shattered the Asherahs and the idols and the molded images and crushed {them}, and he scattered {the dust} upon the faces of the graves of the ones having sacrificed to them.
And he burned the bones of the priests on their altars. And he cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
And in the cities of Manasseh and Ephraim and Simeon and unto Naphtali, in their ruins all around,
he also tore down the altars, and he crushed the Asherahs and the idols to grinding, and he cut apart all of the sun images in all of the land of Israel. And he returned to Jerusalem.

And in the year of 18 to his reigning, for cleansing the land and the house, he sent Shaphan, the son of Azaliah, and Maaseiah, the prince of the city, and Joah, the son of Joahaz, the recorder, to strengthen the house of Yahweh his God.

And they came to Hilkiah, the great priest, and they gave {him} the silver having been brought {to} the house of God that the Levites, the keepers of the threshold, had gathered from the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim and from all of the remnant of Israel and from all of Judah and Benjamin and the dwellers of Jerusalem.

And they gave {it} into the hand of the doer of the work, the ones appointed over the house of Yahweh. And they gave it {to} the doers of the work who were working on the house of Yahweh to repair and to strengthen the house.
And they gave {it} to the craftsmen and the builders to buy stones of hewing and wood for braces and to beam the houses that the kings of Judah had destroyed.

And the men were working in faithfulness in the work. And Jahath and Obadiah, Levites from the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam from the sons of the Kohathites were appointed to supervise over them (now the Levites {were} all understanding in instruments of song}
and over the bearers and overseers for every doer of the work for service and service. And from the Levites {were} scribes and officials and gatekeepers.
And when they were bringing out the silver having been brought {to} the house of Yahweh, Hilkiah the priest found the scroll of the law of Yahweh by the hand of Moses.
And Hilkiah answered and said to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the scroll of the law in the house of Yahweh.” And Hilkiah gave the scroll to Shaphan.
And Shaphan brought the scroll to the king, and he returned a further word {to} the king, saying, “All that was put into the hand of your servants, they are doing.
And they have poured out the silver found in the house of Yahweh, and they have given it into the hand of the appointed ones and into the hand of the doers of the work.”
And Shaphan the scribe declared to the king, saying, “Hilkiah the priest has given a scroll to me.” And Shaphan read from it to the face of the king.
And it happened when the king heard the words of the law that he tore his clothes.
And the king commanded Hilkiah and Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, and Abdon, the son of Micah, and Shaphan the scribe and Asaiah, the servant of the king, saying,

“Go, seek Yahweh for me and for the remnant in Israel and in Judah concerning the words of the scroll that has been found. For great {is} the heat of Yahweh that is poured out on us because our fathers have not kept the word of Yahweh to do like everything written on this scroll.”

And Hilkiah and {those} whom the king {had sent} went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum, the son of Tokhath, the son of Hasrah, the keeper of the garments. And she was dwelling in Jerusalem, in the Second. And they spoke to her like this.
And she said to them, “Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, ‘Say to the man who sent you to me,
“Thus says Yahweh, ‘Behold me, bringing disaster upon this place and upon its dwellers, all of the curses written on the scroll that they read to the face of the king of Judah,
because they have abandoned me and burned incense to other gods so as to provoke me by all of the works of their hands. And my heat will pour out on this place, and it will not extinguish.’”’
But to the king of Judah, the one having sent you to seek Yahweh, thus you shall say to him, ‘Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, {about} the words that you heard,

“Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself from the face of God when you heard his words about this place and about its dwellers, and you have humbled yourself to my face, and you have torn your clothes, and you have wept to my face, so also I, I have heard”—the declaration of Yahweh—

“behold me, gathering you to your fathers. And you will be gathered to your grave in peace, and your eyes will not see all of the disaster that I am bringing on this place and on its dwellers.”’” And they brought back word to the king.
And the king sent, and he assembled all of the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

And the king went up {to} the house of Yahweh, and every man of Judah and the dwellers of Jerusalem and the priests and the Levites and all of the people, from great and to small. And he read in their ears all of the words of the scroll of the covenant having been found in the house of Yahweh.

And the king stood in his place, and he cut a covenant to the face of Yahweh to walk after Yahweh and to keep his commandments, and his testimonies and his statutes with all of his heart and with all of his soul, to do the words of the covenant written on this scroll.
And he made every one found in Jerusalem and Benjamin stand. And the dwellers of Jerusalem did according to the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.

And Josiah removed all of the abominations from all of the lands that {were} to the sons of Israel. And he made every one found in Israel serve, to serve Yahweh, their God. All of his days, they did not turn away from after Yahweh, the God of their fathers.
And Josiah made a Passover in Jerusalem to Yahweh. And they slaughtered the Passover on 14 to the first month.
And he stationed the priests over their keepings, and he strengthened them for the service of the house of Yahweh.

And he said to the Levites teaching all of Israel, {ones} holy to Yahweh, “Put the Holy Box in the house that Solomon, the son of David, the king of Israel, built. {May it} not {be} to you a burden on your shoulder. Now serve Yahweh your God and his people Israel,
and prepare yourselves, by the house of your fathers, according to your divisions, by the writing of David, the king of Israel, and by the writing of Solomon his son,
and stand in the holy place according to the divisions of the house of the fathers of your brothers, the sons of the people, and the portion of the house of a father of the Levites,
and slaughter the Passover, and consecrate yourselves, and prepare for your brothers, to do according to the word of Yahweh by the hand of Moses.”

And Josiah contributed for the sons of the people a flock of lambs and sons of female goats, the whole of the Passovers for all of the ones being found, to the number of 30,000, and 3,000 oxen. These {were} from the property of the king.

And his princes contributed to a freewill offering for the people, for the priests, and for the Levites. Hilkiah and Zechariah and Jehiel, leaders of the house of God, gave to the priests for the Passovers 2,600 {sheep} and 300 oxen.
And Konaniah and Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers and Hashabiah and Jeiel and Jozabad, princes of the Levites, contributed for the Levites for the Passovers, 5,000 {sheep} and 300 oxen.
And the service was prepared, and the priests stood at their station, and the Levites, by their divisions, according to the commandment of the king.
And they slaughtered the Passover, and the priests sprinkled from their hand, and the Levites were skinning.

And they removed the burnt offering to give them to the divisions of the house of the fathers for the sons of the people to bring near to Yahweh, as written in the scroll of Moses. And thus for the oxen.
And they cooked the Passover in fire according to the regulation, but they cooked the holy {things} in pots and in kettles and in pans, and they ran {them} to all of the sons of the people.

And afterward they prepared for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the sons of Aaron, {were} in the offering of the burnt offering and the fat portions until night, so the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.

And the singers, the sons of Asaph, {were} at their station, according to the commandment of David and Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun, the seer of the king, and the gatekeepers, for gate and gate. It was not to them to turn aside from at their station, because their brothers, the Levites, prepared for them.
And all of the service of Yahweh was prepared on that day to make the Passover and to offer burnt offerings on the altar of Yahweh, according to the commandment of King Josiah.
And the sons of Israel being found made the Passover at that time, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, seven days.

Now a Passover like it had not been made in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet. And all of the kings of Israel had not made like the Passover that Josiah made and the priests and the Levites and all of Judah and Israel being found and the dwellers of Jerusalem.
In the year 18 to the reign of Josiah, this Passover was made.
After all of this, when Josiah prepared the house, Neco, the king of Egypt, went up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates. And Josiah went out to meet him.

And he sent messengers to him, saying, “What to me and to you, King of Judah? Not against you, you, today, but against the house of my battle. And God has said for me to hasten. Stop yourself from God, who {is} with me, that he may not destroy you.”
But Josiah did not turn his face from him. But to fight with him, he disguised himself. And he did not listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God. And he came to fight on the plain of Megiddo.
And the shooters shot King Josiah, and the king said to his servants, “Take me away, for I have been wounded badly.”

And his servants took him away from the chariot, and they made him ride on the second chariot that {was} to him. And they brought him {to} Jerusalem. And he died, and he was buried in the graves of his fathers. And all of Judah and Jerusalem were mourning for Josiah.

And Jeremiah lamented for Josiah, and all of the male singers and the female singers have spoken in their laments about Josiah to today. And they made them a statute for Israel, and behold them, written in the laments.
Now the rest of the matters of Josiah and his covenant faithfulnesses as written in the law of Yahweh
and his matters, the first {ones} and the last {ones}, behold them, written on the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah.
And the people of the land took Jehoahaz, the son of Josiah, and they made him reign in Jerusalem in place of his father.
Joahaz {was} a son of 23 years when he reigned, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.
And the king of Egypt removed him in Jerusalem, and he fined the land 100 kikkars of silver and a kikkar of gold.
And the king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother reign over Judah and Jerusalem, and he changed his name {to} Jehoiakim. But Neco took his brother Joahaz and brought him to Egypt.
Jehoiakim {was} a son of 25 years when he reigned, and he reigned 11 years in Jerusalem. And he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh his God.
Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, came up against him, and he bound him with {two} bronze {chains} to bring him to Babylon.
And Nebuchadnezzar brought some of the vessels of the house of Yahweh to Babylon, and he put them in his temple in Babylon.

Now the rest of the matters of Jehoiakim and the abominations that he did and {the thing} found against him, behold them, written on the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah. And Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.
Jehoiachin {was} a son of eight years when he reigned; and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. And he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh.
And at the return of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Babylon, with vessels of delight of the house of Yahweh And he made Zedekiah his brother reign over Judah and Jerusalem.
Zedekiah {was} a son of 21 years when he reigned, and he reigned 11 years in Jerusalem.
And he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh his God. He did not humble himself from the face of Jeremiah the prophet from the mouth of Yahweh.
And he also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God. And he stiffened his neck and he hardened his heart from turning to Yahweh, the God of Israel.

Also all of the princes of the priests and the people made great to transgress transgression like all of the abominations of the nations. And they defiled the house of Yahweh, which he had made holy in Jerusalem.
And Yahweh, the God of their fathers, sent to them by the hand of his messengers, rising early and sending, because he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling.
But they were mocking the messengers of God and despising his words and mistreating his prophets, until the heat of Yahweh went up against his people, until there was no healing.

And he brought up the king of the Chaldeans against them, and he killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and he did not pity a young man or a virgin, old or grey-haired. He gave all into his hand.
All of the vessels of the house of God, the great and the small, and the treasures of the house of Yahweh and the treasures of the king and his princes, he brought all {to} Babylon.
And they burned the house of God, and they tore down the wall of Jerusalem; and they burned all of its citadels with fire, and they destroyed all of its vessels of delight.
And the remnant from the sword, he exiled to Babylon, and they were servants to him and to his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia
to fulfill the word of Yahweh by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed its Sabbaths. It rested all of the days of its being desolated to fulfill 70 years.

And in the year of one to Cyrus, the king of Persia, to accomplish the word of Yahweh by the mouth of Jeremiah, Yahweh awakened the spirit of Cyrus, the king of Persia, and he made a voice pass through all of his kingdom and also in writing, saying,

“Thus says Cyrus, the king of Persia: ‘Yahweh, the God of the heavens, has given all of the kingdoms of the earth to me. And he, he has appointed me to build a house for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever among you {is} from all of his people, {may} Yahweh his God {be} with him, and let him go up.’”

Now in year one of Cyrus, the king of Persia, in order to accomplish the word of Yahweh from the mouth of Jeremiah, Yahweh stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, the king of Persia. So he caused a sound to pass throughout all his kingdom, and also in writing, saying:

“Thus says Cyrus, the king of Persia: Yahweh, the God of heaven, has given to me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he himself has appointed me to build for him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.

Whoever among you is from all his people, may his God be with him, and may he go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and may he build the house of Yahweh, the God of Israel. He is the God who is in Jerusalem.

And every one who is remaining in all of the places where he is sojourning there, let the men of his place lift him with silver and with gold, and with goods and with livestock, along with the freewill offering for the house of God, which is in Jerusalem.”

Then the heads of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, that is, all whose spirit God had stirred up, arose to go up to build the house of Yahweh, which is in Jerusalem.
And all those around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, and with livestock, and with precious gifts, apart from all that was freely offered.
And the king Cyrus brought out the vessels of the house of Yahweh that Nebuchadnezzar had brought out from Jerusalem and had put in the house of his gods.
And Cyrus, the king of Persia, brought them out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer. And he counted them out to Sheshbazzar, the ruler of Judah.
And this was their number: 30 basins of gold, 1,000 basins of silver, 29 knives,
30 bowls of gold, 410 bowls of silver of a second kind, and 1,000 other vessels.
All the vessels of gold and of silver were 5,400. Sheshbazzar brought up all this with the going up of the exiles from Babylon to Jerusalem.

Now these are the sons of the province, the ones who went up from the captivity of the exiles whom Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, had exiled to Babylon. And they returned to Jerusalem and Judah, a man to his city;
who came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah. This is the number of the men of the people of Israel.
The sons of Pahath-Moab, of the sons of Jeshua and Joab were 2, 812.
The sons of Ater, of Hezekiah were 98.
The sons of Kirjath-Arim, Kephirah, and Beeroth were 743.
The sons of the Ramah and Geba were 621.
The men of Bethel and the Ai were 223.
The sons of the other Elam were 1, 254.
The sons of Lod, Hadid, and Ono were 725.
The priests: the sons of Jedaiah of the house of Jeshua were 973.
The Levites: the sons of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodaviah, were 74.
The singers: the sons of Asaph were 128.
The sons of the gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, and the sons of Shobai were 139 in all.
The temple servants: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth,
the sons of Keros, the sons of Siaha, the sons of Padon,
the sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagabah, the sons of Akkub,
the sons of Hagab, the sons of Shalmai, and the sons of Hanan,
the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar, the sons of Reaiah,
the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda, the sons of Gazzam,
the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah, the sons of Besai,
the sons of Asnah, the sons of Meunim, the sons of Nephusim,
the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur,
the sons of Bazluth, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha,
the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah,
the sons of Neziah, and the sons of Hatipha.
The sons of the servants of Solomon: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Hassophereth, the sons of Peruda,
the sons of Jaalah, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel,
the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth Hazzebaim, and the sons of Ami.
All the temple servants and the sons of the servants of Solomon were 392.
And these were the ones who went up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Kerub, Addon, and Immer; but they were not able to tell the house of their fathers or their seed, whether they were from Israel.
The sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, and the sons of Nekoda were 652.
And from the sons of the priests: the sons of Habaiah; the sons of Hakkoz; and the sons of Barzillai, who took a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, so he was called by their name.
These ones sought their record among the ones who were enrolled by genealogy, but they were not found. And they were desecrated from the priesthood.
And the Tirshatha said to them that they must not eat from the holiest holy food until a priest stood with Urim and with Thummim.
All the assembly, as one, was 42, 360:
apart from their male servants and their female servants, these were 7, 337; and for them were 200 men who sang and women who sang.
Their horses were 736. Their mules were 245.
Their camels were 435. Their donkeys were 6, 720.
And when some from the heads of the fathers came to the house of Yahweh which is in Jerusalem, they freely gave for the house of God to cause it to stand upon its place.
They gave according to their ability to the treasury of the work: 61,000 gold darics, and 5,000 silver minas, and 100 tunics of the priests.
So the priests, and the Levites, and some from the people, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the temple servants dwelt in their cities. So all Israel was in their cities.
Then the seventh month came and the sons of Israel were in their cities. And the people were gathered together as one man to Jerusalem.

Then arose Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and his brothers, and they built the altar of the God of Israel to offer up burnt up offerings on it as is written in the law of Moses, the man of God.

And they set up the altar on its foundation, for dread was on them because of the peoples of the lands. Then they offered up on it burnt up offerings to Yahweh, burnt up offerings at the morning and at the evening.
Then they made the Festival of Huts as is written, with a burnt up offering day by day, by number according to the ordinance of the matter of the day, on its day.
And after this was a continual burnt up offering, and for the new moons, and for all the consecrated appointed times of Yahweh, and for everyone who freely offered a freewill offering to Yahweh.
From day one of the seventh month they began to offer up burnt up offerings to Yahweh, but the temple of Yahweh had not been founded.

And they gave silver to the masons and to the carpenters, and food, and drink, and oil to the Sidonians and to the Tyrians, to bring trees of cedar from Lebanon to the sea of Joppa, according to the permission of Cyrus, the king of Persia, given to them.

Then in the second year of their coming to the house of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and the rest of their brothers the priests and the Levites, and all the ones who came from captivity to Jerusalem began, and they appointed the Levites from a son of 20 years and above to act as overseers for the work of the house of Yahweh.

And Jeshua, his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, stood as one to act as overseers for the ones doing the work at the house of God, the sons of Henadad, their sons, and their brothers the Levites.

Then the ones who were building laid the foundation of the temple of Yahweh. And they caused to stand the clothed priests with the trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with the cymbals, to praise Yahweh in accordance with the hands of David, the king of Israel.

Then they sang in response, praising and giving thanks to Yahweh: “For he is good, for his covenant faithfulness to Israel is to eternity!” And all the people shouted a great shout in praise to Yahweh because the foundation of the house of Yahweh had been laid.

But many from the priests and the Levites, and the heads of the fathers, the old men who had seen the first house, at the founding of this house in their eyes, were weeping with a loud voice. Yet many with a shout, with joy, were lifting up a voice.

So the people could not differentiate the sound of the shout of joy from the sound of the weeping of the people. For the people were shouting a great shout, and the sound was heard as far as from a remote place.
Now the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the sons of the exile were building a temple for Yahweh, the God of Israel.

So they came to Zerubbabel and to the heads of the fathers and they said to them, “Let us build with you, for, like you, we seek your God and to him we have been sacrificing since the days of Esarhaddon, the king of Assyria, the one who caused us to come up here.”

But Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of the fathers of Israel said to them, “It is not for you and for us to build a house for our God, but we ourselves together will build for Yahweh, the God of Israel, just as the king Cyrus, the king of Persia, has commanded us.”
And it happened that the people of the land were making the hands of the people of Judah weak, and making them afraid to build,
and hiring counselors against them to frustrate their plans all the days of Cyrus, the king of Persia, and until the reign of Darius, the king of Persia.
Now in the reign of Ahasuerus, in the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against those who dwelled in Judah and Jerusalem.

And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel and the rest of his companions wrote to Artaxerxes, the king of Persia, and the script of the letter was written in Aramaic and was interpreted in Aramaic.
Rehum, a lord of decree, and Shimshai the scribe wrote one letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king as follows:

Then Rehum, a lord of decree, and Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their companions, the judges and the rulers, the officials, the Persians, the Erechites, the Babylonians, the Susaites (that is, the Elamites),
and the rest of the nations whom Ashurbanipal the great and the noble caused to be exiled and caused them to dwell in the cities of Samaria, and the rest of Beyond-the-River. And now:
(This is a copy of the letter that they sent to him.)
let it be known to the king that the Jews who went up from near you have come to us at Jerusalem. Rebuilding the rebellious and evil city, they are completing the walls and repairing the foundations.
Now let it be known to the king that if that city is built and the walls are completed, they will not give tax, tribute, or custom, and the revenue of the kings will suffer harm.
Now, because we have eaten the salt of the palace, and it is not appropriate for us to see the nakedness of the king, on account of this we have sent and made known to the king,

so that he may search in the book of the records of your fathers. And you will discover in the book of the records and learn that that city is a rebellious city and one that has caused harm to kings and provinces, and they have made revolt in its midst since the ancient days. On account of this, that city was destroyed.
We are making known to the king that if that city is built and the walls are completed, because of this there will be no share for you in Beyond-the-River.”
The letter that you sent to us has been carefully read aloud before me.
So from me was set a decree, and they searched and discovered that that city since the ancient days has risen up against kings and rebellion and revolt have been made in it.
And mighty kings were over Jerusalem, even rulers over all of Beyond the River; and tax, tribute, and custom were paid to them.
Now, set a decree to stop these men, so that city may not be rebuilt until the decree is set from me.
And be careful of negligence of action concerning this. Why should the damage increase to the harm of the kings?”

Then from when the copy of the letter of Artaxerxes the king was read aloud before Rehum, and Shimshai the scribe, and their companions, they went in a hurry to Jerusalem against the Jews, and they stopped them by an arm and strength.
At that time the work of the house of God which is in Jerusalem stopped, and it was stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius, the king of Persia.
Then the prophets, Haggai the prophet and Zechariah, the son of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews who were in Judah and in Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel who was over them.
Then Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, arose and began to build the house of God which is in Jerusalem, and the prophets of God were with them, supporting them.

At that time, Tattenai, the governor of Beyond-the-River, and Shethar-Bozenai, and their companions came to them and spoke to them thus, “Who set for you a decree to build this house and to complete this structure?”
Then accordingly we said to them, “What are the names of the men who are building this building?”
But the eye of God was on the elders of the Jews, and they did not stop them until the report came to Darius, and then they returned the letter concerning this matter.
A copy of the letter that Tattenai, the governor of Beyond-the-River, and Shethar-Bozenai and his companions, the officials who were in Beyond-the-River, sent to Darius the king.
They sent a report to him and thus was written within it:

Let it be known to the king that we went to Judah, the province, to the house of the great God, and it is being built of large stones, and timber is being placed in the walls. And this work is being done diligently and is succeeding in their hand.
Then we asked these elders, we said thus to them, ‘Who set a decree for you to build this house and to complete this structure?’
And also we asked of them their names, to let you know, so that we could write down the names of the men who were at their head.

And thus is the answer they returned us, saying, ‘We are servants of him who is the God of heaven and earth, and we are building the house that was built many years before this, and a great king of Israel built it and completed it.

However, because of this, that our fathers caused the God of heaven to be angry, he gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, the Chaldean, and he destroyed this house and caused the people to be exiled to Babylon.
But in year one of Cyrus, the king of Babylon, Cyrus the king set a decree to build this house of God.

And also the vessels of the house of God, of gold and silver, that Nebuchadnezzar had taken out from the temple that was in Jerusalem and had brought them to the temple of Babylon—Cyrus the king took them out from the temple of Babylon and they were given to one whose name was Sheshbazzar, whom he had set as governor.
Then he said to him, “Take away these vessels. Go deposit them in the temple that is in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be built on its place.”
Then that Sheshbazzar came; he laid the foundation of the house of God which is in Jerusalem. And from then even until now it is being built, but it is not complete.’

And now, if it is good to the king, let a search be made in the house of the treasures of the king which is there in Babylon, if it is that a decree was set by Cyrus the king to build this house of God in Jerusalem. And let him send to us the will of the king concerning this.”
Then Darius the king set a decree and they searched in the house of the books where the treasures had been deposited there in Babylon.
And one scroll was found in the fortress at Ecbatana that is in the province of Media, and the record was written within it thusly:
“In year one of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king set a decree about the house of God in Jerusalem:
with three layers of large stone and a layer of new timber. And let the cost be given from the house of the king.

And also, the vessels of the house of God, of gold and silver, that Nebuchadnezzar had taken out from the temple that was in Jerusalem and had brought to Babylon, must be returned. And let each go to the temple that is in Jerusalem, to its place. So you must put them in the house of God.’”
“Now Tattenai, the governor of Beyond-the-River, Shethar-Bozenai, and their companions, the officials who are in Beyond-the-River: be far away from there.
Leave alone the work of that house of God. Let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build that house of God on its place.

And from me is set a decree for what it is that you shall do with these elders of the Jews to build that house of God. And from the treasures of the king (that is, the tribute of Beyond-the-River) let the expense be given to those men diligently, so that it does not stop.

And whatever is needed (whether sons of bulls, or rams, or lambs for burnt up offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine, or oil, according to the command of the priests who are in Jerusalem), let it be given to them day by day (that is, without neglect),
so that they may be offering sweet-smelling sacrifices to the God of heaven and praying for the life of the king and his sons.

And from me is set a decree that, for any man who changes this edict, a beam shall be pulled from his house, and, being erect, he shall be impaled on it. And his house shall be made a rubbish heap on account of this.

And may the God who has caused his name to dwell there overthrow any king or people who stretches out his hand to change, to destroy that house of God which is in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have set a decree. Let it be done diligently.”
Then Tattenai, the governor of Beyond-the-River, Shethar-Bozenai, and their companions did thus diligently, according to what Darius the king had sent.

And the elders of the Jews were building and prospering by the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. And they built and completed by the decree of the God of Israel and by the decree of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes, the king of Persia.
And this house was done by day three of the month of Adar, which was year six of the reign of Darius the king.
And the sons of Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the rest of the sons of the exile performed the dedication of this house of God with joy.
And they offered for the dedication of this house of God 100 bulls, 200 rams, 400 lambs, and 12 bucks of goats for a sin offering for all Israel, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
And they caused the priests to stand in their divisions, and the Levites in their sections, for the service of the God who is in Jerusalem, according to the writing of the book of Moses.
So the sons of the exile made the Passover on day 14 of the first month.

For the priests and the Levites had purified themselves as one, all of them were pure. And they slaughtered the Passover for all the sons of the exile, and for their brothers, the priests, and for themselves.

And the sons of Israel ate, the ones who had returned from the exile and every one who separated himself to them from the uncleanness of the nations of the land in order to seek Yahweh, the God of Israel.

Then they made the Festival of Unleavened Bread seven days with joy, because Yahweh had caused them to be joyful, and had caused the heart of the king of Assyria to turn toward them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of God, the God of Israel.
Now after these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes, the king of Persia: Ezra (the son of Seraiah, the son of Azariah, the son of Hilkiah,
the son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub,
the son of Amariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth,
the son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki,
the son of Abishua, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the head priest),

this Ezra went up from Babylon, and he was a skilled scribe in the law of Moses that Yahweh, the God of Israel, had given. And the king granted to him all his request according to the hand of Yahweh his God upon him.
And some from the sons of Israel and from the priests, and the Levites, and the ones who sang, and the gatekeepers, and the temple servants went up to Jerusalem in year seven of Artaxerxes the king.
And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was in the seventh year of the king.
For on the first of the first month was the beginning of the ascent from Babylon. And on the first of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God upon him.
For Ezra had made his heart firm to seek the law of Yahweh, and to do it, and to teach statute and ordinance in Israel.
Now this is a copy of the letter that the king Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe, a scribe of the words of the commandments of Yahweh and his statutes for Israel:
“Artaxerxes, the king of kings, to Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven: Peace. And now:
from me is set a decree that everyone in my kingdom who freely offers to go to Jerusalem with you, from the people ‘Israel’ and its priests and the Levites, may go.
Because it was sent from before the king and his seven counselors to inquire about Judah and about Jerusalem by the law of your God which is in your hand,
and to bring silver and gold that the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,

with all the silver and the gold that you find in all the province of Babylon, along with the freewill offering of the people and the priests who freely give for the house of God, which is in Jerusalem:

therefore, diligently you shall buy with this money bulls, rams, lambs, and their grain offerings and their drink offerings; and you shall offer them on the altar of the house of your God, which is in Jerusalem.
And you may do whatever seems good to you and to your brothers to do with the rest of the silver and the gold, according to the will of your God.
And the vessels that were given to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver in full before the God of Jerusalem.
And the rest of what is needed for the house of your God that falls to you to give, you may give from the house of the treasures of the king.

And from me myself, Artaxerxes the king, is set a decree for all the treasurers who are in Beyond-the-River: that all that Ezra (the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven) may ask of you, let it be done diligently;
as much as 100 silver kikkars, and as much as 100 cors of wheat, and as much as 100 baths of wine, and as much as 100 baths of oil, and salt which is not written.
Everything that is from the decree of the God of heaven shall be done exactly for the house of the God of heaven. For why should there be wrath against the kingdom of the king and his sons?

And to you is made known that there is no authority to set tax, tribute, or custom upon all the priests, and the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, the temple servants, and the servants of that house of God.

And as for you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God that is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges who may judge all the people who are in Beyond-the-River, all who know the laws of your God. And you shall teach those who do not know.

And everyone who will not do the law of your God and the law of the king, judgment shall be exacted from him diligently, whether for death, whether for banishment, whether for confiscation of goods, or for imprisonment.”
Blessed be Yahweh, the God of our fathers, who gave according to this in the heart of the king, to glorify the house of Yahweh, which is in Jerusalem,

and caused covenant faithfulness to extend to me before the face of the king, and his counselors, and before all the mighty officials of the king. And as for me, I gained strength according to the hand of Yahweh my God upon me, and I gathered from Israel heads to go up with me.
Now these are the heads of their fathers and their enrollment by genealogy, the ones who went up with me from Babylon in the reign of Artaxerxes the king:
From the sons of Phinehas: Gershom.
From the sons of Pahath-Moab: Eliehoenai, the son of Zerahiah, and with him were 200 males.
From the sons of … Shecaniah the son of Jahaziel, and with him were 300 males.
And from the sons of Adin: Ebed, the son of Jonathan, and with him were 50 males.
And from the sons of Elam: Jeshaiah, the son of Athaliah, and with him were 70 males.
And from the sons of Shephatiah: Zebadiah, the son of Michael, and with him were 80 males.
From the sons of Joab: Obadiah, the son of Jehiel, and with him were 218 males.
And from the sons of … Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him were 160 males.
And from the sons of Bebai: Zechariah, the son of Bebai, and with him were 28 males.
And from the sons of Azgad: Johanan, the son of Hakkatan, and with him were 110 males.
And from the last sons of Adonikam, and these were their names: Eliphelet, Jeuel, and Shemaiah, and with them were 60 males.
And from the sons of Bigvai: Uthai and Zaccur, and with him were 70 males.
And I gathered them to the river, the one that goes to Ahava, and we encamped there three days. And I examined the people and the priests, but I did not find there any from the sons of Levi.

Then I sent for Eliezer, for Ariel, for Shemaiah, and for Elnathan, and for Jarib, and for Elnathan and for Nathan, and for Zechariah, and for Meshullam, the heads; and for Joiarib, and for Elnathan, men of understanding.

And I commanded them to go to Iddo, the head at the place Kasiphia. And I put in their mouth words to speak to Iddo and his brothers, the temple servants in the place Kasiphia, to bring to us those who minister for the house of our God.

And according to the good hand of our God upon us, they brought to us: a man of insight from the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel, even Sherebiah, and his sons and his brothers were 18;
and Hashabiah, and with him, Jeshaiah, from the sons of Merari, whose brothers and their sons were 20;
and 220 temple servants from the temple servants whom David with the officials had given for the service of the Levites. All of them were designated by names.
Then I proclaimed a fast there at the river Ahava, to afflict ourselves before the face of our God to seek from him a straight way for us, and for our children, and for all our property.

For I was ashamed to ask from the king an army and horsemen to help us from an enemy on the way. For we had spoken to the king, saying, “The hand of our God is for good upon all those who seek him, but his might and his nose are against all those who forsake him.”
So we fasted and sought from our God concerning this, and he was entreated by us.
Then I separated 12 from the leaders of the priests to Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and with them ten from their brothers.

And I weighed out to them the silver and the gold and the vessels, the offering of the house of our God that the king, and his counselors, and his officials, and all Israel (the ones who were found) had offered.
And I weighed out to their hand 650 kikkars of silver, and vessels of silver of 100 kikkars, 100 kikkars of gold,
and 20 bowls of gold of 1,000 darics, and two good, gleaming vessels of bronze, precious as gold.
And I said to them, “You are holy to Yahweh, and the vessels are holy. And the silver and the gold are a freewill offering to Yahweh, the God of your fathers.
Watch and keep until you weigh them out before the face of the leaders of the priests and the Levites and the leaders of the fathers of Israel, at Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of Yahweh.”
So the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, to bring them to Jerusalem, to the house of our God.
Then we set out from the river Ahava on day 12 of the first month to go to Jerusalem. And the hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the palm of the enemy and ambush on the way.
So we came to Jerusalem, and we stayed there three days.

And on the fourth day, the silver and the gold and the vessels were weighed out: in the house of our God into the hand of Meremoth, the son of Uriah, the priest, and with him was Eleazar, the son of Phinehas (and with them were Jozabad, the son of Jeshua, and Noadiah, the son of Binnui, the Levites);
by number and weight of everything. And all the weight was written at that time.

The ones who had come from the captivity, the sons of the exile, offered burnt up offerings to the God of Israel: 12 bulls for all Israel, 96 rams, 77 lambs, 12 male goats of a sin offering. The whole was a burnt up offering to Yahweh.
And they gave the laws of the king to the satraps of the king and the governors of Beyond-the-River. And they lifted the people and the house of God.

Now as soon as these things were finished, the leaders came to me, saying, “The people of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands according to their abominations, of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, the Ammonite, the Moabite, the Egyptian, and the Amorite.

For they have lifted from their daughters for themselves and for their sons, so they have mixed the seed of holiness with the peoples of the lands. And the hand of the leaders and the rulers has been first in this unfaithfulness.”
And as soon as I heard this matter, I tore my garment and my robe. And I pulled out some from the hair of my head and my beard, and I sat down appalled.
And all who trembled at the words of the God of Israel on account of the unfaithfulness of the exiles were gathered to me. And I was sitting appalled until the offering of the evening.
And at the offering of the evening I arose from my humiliation, and when I tore my garment and my robe. And I knelt down on my knees, and spread out my palms to Yahweh my God.
And I said, “My God, I am ashamed and humiliated to raise my face to you, my God. For our iniquities have multiplied to above the head, and our guilt has grown up as far as to the heavens.

From the days of our fathers until this day we are in great guilt. And in our iniquities, we ourselves, our kings, and our priests have been given into the hand of the kings of the lands by sword, by captivity, and by plunder, and by shame of face, as this day.

But now, according to a little moment, favor has come from with Yahweh our God to leave for us survivors and to give to us a peg in his holy place, for our God to brighten our eyes and to give us a little reviving in our slavery.

For we are slaves, yet our God has not forsaken us in our slavery. But he has extended to us covenant faithfulness before the face of the kings of Persia to give to us reviving, to raise up the house of our God and to cause its ruins to stand, and to give to us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.
So now, our God, what can we say after this? For we have forsaken your commandments,

which you commanded by the hand of your servants, the prophets, saying, ‘The land that you are entering to possess is a land of impurity by the impurity of the peoples of the lands, by their abominations that have filled it from mouth to mouth with their uncleanness.

So now, neither give your daughters to their sons nor lift their daughters for your sons, nor shall you seek their peace or their good until eternity, so that you may be strong and eat the good things of the land and cause your sons to inherit it until eternity.’

Yet after all that has come upon us because of our evil deeds and because of our great guilt (although you, our God, you have restrained it to lower than our iniquities, and you have given to us a survival such as this),
