the one making destruction flash against the strong, and destruction comes against the fortress.
They hate the reprover in the gate, and they abhor the one speaking blamelessly.

Therefore, because of your trampling on the poor and you take a tax of grain from him: you have built houses of hewn stone, but you will not dwell in them; you have planted vineyards of desire, but you will not drink their wine.
For I know your transgressions {are} many, and your sins {are} mighty— oppressors of the righteous, takers of a bribe, and they turn aside the needy in the gate.
Therefore the prudent will be still in that time, for it {is} an evil time.
Seek good, and not evil, so that you may live; and thus may Yahweh, God of Armies, be with you, just as you have said.
Hate evil, and love good, and establish justice in the gate; perhaps Yahweh, God of Armies, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore thus says Yahweh, God of Armies, the Lord, “In all plazas {there will be} wailing, and in all streets they will say, ‘Alas! Alas!’ And they will call the farmer to mourning, and wailing to those knowing a lament.
And in all the vineyards {there will be} wailing, for I will pass through your midst,” says Yahweh.
Woe to the ones desiring the day of Yahweh! What {is} this to you, the day of Yahweh? It {is} darkness and not light.
As when a man flees from the face of the lion, and the bear meets him; or goes into the house and rests his hand on the wall, and the snake bites him.
{Is} not the day of Yahweh darkness, and not light? Even gloom, with no brightness in it?
“I hate, I reject your feasts, and I will not smell in your assemblies.
For if you offer up to me burnt offerings and your grain offerings, I will not accept {them}; and the peace offering of your fattened animals, I will not look at.
Remove from me the noise of your songs; and the music of your harps I will not hear.
But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.
Did you bring near to me sacrifices and a grain offering in the wilderness forty years, house of Israel?
But you carried Sikkuth your king, and Kiyyun your images, the star of your gods, which you made for yourselves.
So I will exile you from farther than Damascus,” says Yahweh, God of Armies {is} his name.
Woe to the ones at ease in Zion, and {to} the ones trusting in the mountain of Samaria, designated {ones} of the first of the nations —and to them the house of Israel comes!
Cross over to Calneh and see, and go from there to Hamath Rabbah, and go down to Gath of the Philistines. {Are} they better than these kingdoms? Or {is} their border greater than your border?
—the ones putting far off the evil day, but you bring near a seat of violence;
—the ones lying on beds of ivory, and sprawling on their couches, and eating young rams from the flock, and calves from the midst of the stall;
—the ones improvising on the mouth of the harp; like David they devised for themselves instruments of song;
—the ones drinking from bowls of wine, and they anoint {themselves} with the first of oils, but they are not grieved over the breaking of Joseph.
Therefore, now they will go into exile at the head of the exiles, and the revelry of the sprawling ones will depart.
The Lord Yahweh has sworn by his soul—the declaration of Yahweh, the God of Armies— “I am abhorring the pride of Jacob, and his citadels I hate, and I will give over a city and its fullness.”
And it will happen, if ten men remain in one house, then they will die.

And his kinsman and the one burning him will lift him up to bring out the bones from the house, and he will say to the one who {is} in the innermost parts of the house, “Is there yet {anyone} with you?” and he will say, “None.” Then he will say, “Hush! For not to make mention of the name of Yahweh.”
For, behold, Yahweh is commanding, and he will strike the great house into fragments, and the small house into fissures.
Do horses run on the cliff? Or does one plow {it} with oxen? For you have turned justice into poisonweed, and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood;
—the ones rejoicing over Lo Debar, the ones saying, “Have we not by our strength taken Karnaim for ourselves?”
“For behold me raising up against you, house of Israel”—the declaration of Yahweh, the God of Armies— “a nation, and they will oppress you, from Lebo Hamath to the brook of the Arabah.”

Thus the Lord Yahweh made me see, and behold, {he} was forming a locust swarm at the beginning of the coming up of the latter growth. And behold, the latter growth {was} after the mowings of the king.
And it happened, when it had finished eating the vegetation of the land, that I said, “Lord Yahweh, please forgive! How will Jacob stand? For he {is} small.”
Yahweh relented concerning this. “It will not be,” said Yahweh.
Thus the Lord Yahweh made me see, and behold, the Lord Yahweh was calling to contend by fire. And it devoured the great deep and was devouring the portion.
And I said, “Lord Yahweh, please cease! How will Jacob stand? For he {is} small.”
Yahweh relented concerning this. “This also will not be,” said the Lord Yahweh.
Thus he made me see, and behold, the Lord was standing beside a wall of a plumb line, and in his hand {was} a plumb line.

And Yahweh said to me, “What are you seeing, Amos?” And I said, “A plumb line.” And the Lord said, “Behold me placing a plumb line in the midst of my people Israel. I will not again repeat to pass over him.
And the high places of Isaac will be deserted, and the sanctuaries of Israel will be desolate, and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.”
Then Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent to Jeroboam, king of Israel, saying, “Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel. The land is not able to contain all of his words.
For thus Amos says, ‘By the sword Jeroboam will die, and Israel, going into exile, will go into exile from upon his ground.’”
And Amaziah said to Amos, “Seer, go, flee for yourself to the land of Judah, and eat bread there, and there you shall prophesy.
But {at} Bethel you shall not repeat to prophesy again, for it {is} a sanctuary of the king, and it {is} a house of a kingdom.”
And Amos answered and said to Amaziah, “I {am} not a prophet, and I {am} not a son of a prophet, for I {am} a herdsman, and a tender of sycamore figs.
But Yahweh took me from after the flock, and Yahweh said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to my people Israel.’
And now, hear the word of Yahweh. You are saying, ‘You shall not prophesy against Israel, and you shall not drip against the house of Isaac.’

Therefore, thus says Yahweh, ‘Your wife will prostitute herself in the city, and your sons and your daughters will fall by the sword, and your ground will be divided by the measuring line, and you, you will die on unclean ground, and Israel, going into exile, will go into exile from upon his ground.’”
Thus the Lord Yahweh made me see, and behold, a basket of summer fruit!
And he said, “What are you seeing, Amos?” And I said, “A basket of summer fruit.” And Yahweh said to me, “The end has come to my people Israel; I will not repeat again to pass over him.
And the songs of the temple will wail in that day”—the declaration of the Lord Yahweh— “many {are} the corpses; in every place one has thrown {them}. Hush!”
Hear this, the ones trampling the needy and to cause the afflicted of the land to cease,
saying, “When will the new moon pass, that we may sell grain, and the Sabbath, that we may open wheat, to make the ephah small and to make the shekel great, and to pervert balances of deceit,
to buy the poor with silver and the needy in exchange for a pair of sandals, and the refuse of grain we will sell?”
Yahweh has sworn by the pride of Jacob, “If I ever forget all of their deeds.
Will not the land tremble over this, and everyone dwelling in it mourn? And all of it will rise like the Nile, and be cast up and sunk, like the Nile of Egypt.
And it will happen in that day”—the declaration of the Lord Yahweh— “that I will make the sun set at noon, and I will darken the land in a day of light.

And I will turn your feasts into mourning and all of your songs into a lament. And I will bring up sackcloth on all loins, and baldness on every head. And I will make it like the mourning for an only child, and its end like a bitter day.
Behold, days are coming”—the declaration of the Lord Yahweh— “when I will send a famine in the land, not a famine for bread, and not a thirst for water, but rather to hear the words of Yahweh.
And they will stagger from sea to sea, and from the north and to the sunrise; they will rove about to seek the word of Yahweh, but they will not find it.
In that day, the beautiful virgins will faint, and the young men, from thirst—
the ones swearing by the guilt of Samaria, and they say, ‘By the life of your god, Dan!’ and, ‘By the life of the way of Beersheba!’— and they will fall, and they will not rise again.”

I saw the Lord standing by the altar, and he said, “Strike the capital so that the thresholds shake, and cut them off on the head of all of them, and their end I will kill with the sword. A fleeing one will not flee for them, and a fugitive will not escape for them.
If they dig into Sheol, from there my hand will take them. And if they go up to the heavens, from there I will bring them down.

And if they hide themselves in the head of Carmel, from there I will search out and take them. And if they are hidden from before my eyes in the floor of the sea, from there I will command the serpent and it will bite them.
And if they go in captivity to the face of their enemies, from there I will command the sword and it will kill them. And I will set my eye on them for evil and not for good.”
And the Lord Yahweh of Armies, the one touching the earth and it melts, and all of the dwellers in it mourn, and all of it goes up like the Nile, and it sinks like the Nile of Egypt;

the one building his stairs in the heavens, and his vault, over the earth he founded it, the one calling to the waters of the sea, and he pours them out upon the face of the earth— Yahweh {is} his name.
“Are you not like the sons of the Cushites to me, sons of Israel?”—the declaration of Yahweh— “Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?

Behold, the eyes of the Lord Yahweh are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from upon the face of the ground. Nevertheless, destroying, I will not destroy the house of Jacob”—the declaration of Yahweh.
“For behold, I am commanding, and I will shake the house of Israel among all of the nations, just as it is shaken in the sieve, and a pebble will not fall to the earth.
By the sword all of the sinners of my people will die, the ones saying, ‘The evil will not approach or reach as far as us.’
In that day, I will raise up the fallen booth of David, and I will wall up their breaches, and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as {in} the days of antiquity,
so that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all of the nations whom my name is called over them”— the declaration of Yahweh, the one doing this.

“Behold, days are coming”—the declaration of Yahweh— “and the plower will approach the reaper, and the treader of grapes to the sower of the seed, and the mountains will drip sweet wine, and all of the hills will melt.

And I will restore the restoration of my people Israel, and they will build desolated cities and dwell {there}, and they will plant vineyards and drink their wine, and they will make gardens and eat their fruit.
And I will plant them upon their ground, and they will not be uprooted again from upon their ground that I gave to them,” says Yahweh your God.

The vision of Obadiah: thus says my Lord Yahweh concerning Edom. We have heard a message from Yahweh, and a messenger has been sent off among the nations: Get up! And let us rise up against her for battle!
Behold, I am making you small among the nations, you are extremely despised.
The pride of your heart has deceived you: he who dwells in the clefts of the rock, lofty in his dwelling; he who says in his heart, “Who will bring me down to earth?”
If you make yourself high like the eagle, even if your nest is set between the stars, from there I will bring you down: a declaration of Yahweh.
If thieves came to you, and plunderers by night (how you are being destroyed!), would they not steal enough for them? If grape-cutters came to you, would they not leave behind gleanings?
How Esau is being ransacked, his hidden treasures being searched out!

All the men of your covenant are sending you away as far as the border. The men of your peace are deceiving you and are prevailing against you. They of your bread will set a trap under you. There is no understanding in him.
Will I not on that day (a declaration of Yahweh) destroy wise men from Edom, and understanding from the mountain of Esau?
And your mighty men will be dismayed, O Teman, so that a man will be cut off from the mountain of Esau by slaughter.
Because of violence against your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off for eternity.
On the day that you stood opposite, on the day that strangers took captive his wealth, and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem, you also were like one of them.

But you should not have looked on the day of your brother, on the day of his misfortune. And you should not have rejoiced over the sons of Judah in the day of their perishing. And you should not have made your mouth great in a day of distress.

You should not have entered the gate of my people in the day of their calamity. You should not have looked—yes, you!—on his evil in the day of his calamity. And you women should not have looted his wealth in the day of his calamity.
And you should not have stood at the crossroads to cut down his fugitives. And you should not have delivered up his survivors in a day of distress.
For the day of Yahweh is near upon all the nations. According to what you have done, it will be done to you; your recompense will return on your own head.
For according to how you drank on the mountain of my holiness, all the nations shall drink continually. And they will drink, and they will swallow, and they will become like they never existed.
But in the mountain of Zion there will be an escape, and there will be holiness, and the house of Jacob will possess their own possessions.

And the house of Jacob will become a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau as stubble. And they will burn them, and consume them. And there will be no survivor for the house of Esau, for Yahweh has spoken.
And the Negev will possess the mountain of Esau, and the Shephelah, the Philistines. And they will possess the field of Ephraim and the field of Samaria, and Benjamin, Gilead.
And the exile of this army of the sons of Israel, who are Canaanites, as far as Zarephath, and the exile of Jerusalem, who are in Sepharad: they will possess the cities of the Negev.
And saviors will go up to the mountain of Zion to judge the mountain of Esau, and the kingdom will belong to Yahweh.
And the word of Yahweh came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying,
“Get up, go to Nineveh, the great city, and call out against it, because their evil has risen up before my face.”

But Jonah got up to run away to Tarshish from before the face of Yahweh. And he went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish. So he paid the fare and went down into it to go with them to Tarshish, away from before the face of Yahweh.
But Yahweh sent out a great wind on the sea and a great storm happened on the sea, so that the ship was thinking to be broken apart.

Then the sailors were frightened, and they cried out, a man to his god. And they threw the things that were in the ship into the sea to lighten it from upon them. But Jonah had gone down into the innermost parts of the ship, and had lain down, and was deeply asleep.
Then the captain of the crew came to him and said to him, “What to you, sleeping? Get up! Cry out to your god! Maybe that god will notice us, and we will not perish.”
Then they said, a man to his friend, “Come, and let us cast lots, so that we may know on whose account this evil is happening to us.” So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
Then they said to him, “Please tell us on whose account this evil is happening to us. What is your occupation, and where do you come from? What is your country, and from which people are you?”
So he said to them, “I am a Hebrew, and I fear Yahweh, the God of heaven, who has made the sea and the dry land.”
Then the men feared a great fear, and they said to him, “What is this that you have done?” For the men knew that he was running away from before the face of Yahweh, because he had told them.
Then they said to him, “What should we do to you so that the sea will calm down from upon us?” For the sea was progressing and storming.
And he said to them, “Lift me up and throw me into the sea. Then the sea will calm down from upon you, for I know that this great storm is upon you because of me.”
But the men rowed hard to return themselves to the land, but they could not, because the sea was progressing and storming over them.

So they cried out to Yahweh and said, “Ah! Yahweh, please do not let us perish on account of the life of this man, and do not put innocent blood upon us, because you, Yahweh, have done just as you desired.”
So they lifted up Jonah and threw him into the sea, and the sea ceased from its raging.
Then the men feared Yahweh {with} great fear, and they sacrificed a sacrifice to Yahweh and vowed vows.
Now Yahweh appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the abdomen of the fish three days and three nights.
And Jonah prayed to Yahweh his God from the abdomen of the fish.
And he said, “I cried out to Yahweh from my distress, and he answered me. From the belly of Sheol I cried out; you heard my voice.
Now you had cast me {to} the deep, into the heart of the seas, and a current surrounded me; all your billows and your waves passed over me.
But I, I said, ‘I have been driven out from before your eyes; yet I might again look toward the temple of your holiness.’
Water had closed around me even as far as life, the deep was surrounding me; seaweed was wrapped around my head.
I had gone down to the bases of the mountains. The earth, its bars {were} around me forever, but you brought up my life from the pit, Yahweh, my God!
When my life fainted upon me, I remembered Yahweh and my prayer came to you, to the temple of your holiness.
Those who give attention to vanities of worthlessness forsake their covenant faithfulness.
But I, I will sacrifice to you with a voice of thanksgiving; I will fulfill what I have vowed. Salvation belongs to Yahweh!”
And Yahweh spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto the dry land.
Then the word of Yahweh came to Jonah a second time, saying,
“Get up, go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim to it the proclamation that I tell to you.”
So Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, according to the word of Yahweh.
So Jonah began to go into the city a journey of one day, and he called out and said, “Still 40 days, then Nineveh will be overthrown.”
And the men of Nineveh believed God. And they proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.
Then the word came to the king of Nineveh, and he rose up from his throne, and he took off his robe from being on him, and he covered himself {with} sackcloth and sat down on the ash heap.

And he proclaimed and spoke within Nineveh from a decree of the king and his nobles, saying: “The person and the animal, the herd and the flock, must not taste anything; they must not graze, and they must not drink water.
But let the man and the beast be covered {with} sackcloth, and they must cry out to God with strength, and each man must turn back from his evil way and from the violence that is in their hands.
Who knows? This god might turn back and have compassion and relent from the burning of his nose so that we will not perish.”
And God saw their deeds, that they turned away from their evil ways. And God relented in regard to the evil that he had said he would do to them, and he did not do {it}.
But it made evil to Jonah a great evil, and it burned to him.

So he prayed to Yahweh and said, “Ah! Yahweh, was this not my word while I was in my country? Because of this I acted beforehand to flee to Tarshish, because I knew that you are a gracious and compassionate God, long of nostrils and abundant in covenant faithfulness, and one who relents from evil.
So now, Yahweh, I beg you, take my life from me, for my death is better than my life.”
And Yahweh said, “Is it right that it burns to you?”

Then Jonah went out from the city and sat down facing the city from the east. And there he made a shelter for himself, and he sat under it in the shade until he might see what would be within the city.

Then Yahweh God appointed a plant and caused it to grow up from over Jonah to be a shade over his head in order to rescue him from his evil. And Jonah rejoiced with great rejoicing because of the plant.
Then God appointed a worm at the rising of the dawn of the next day; and it attacked the plant, and it withered.

And as soon as the rising of the sun happened, then God appointed a hot east wind; and the sun beat on the head of Jonah, and he became faint. Then he asked his spirit to die and said, “My death is better than my life.”
Then God said to Jonah, “Is it right that it burns to you about the plant?” And he said, “It is right that it burns to me, even as far as death.”
Then Yahweh said, “You, you feel troubled about the plant, for which you did no work, nor did you make it grow; it came as a son of a night, and it perished as a son of a night.
So I, should I not feel troubled about Nineveh, the great city, in which there are more than 120, 000 people who do not know between their right hand to their left hand, and many animals?”
The word of Yahweh that was to Micah the Morashtite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, {and} Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
Hear, peoples, all of them; pay attention, earth, and its fullness, that the Lord Yahweh may be against you as a witness, the Lord from the palace of his holiness.
For behold, Yahweh is going out from his place, and he will come down and tread on the high places of the earth.
And the mountains will melt under him, and the valleys will split open, like wax from the face of the fire, like waters poured down a steep place.

All this {is} because of the transgression of Jacob, and because of the sins of the house of Israel. Who {is} the transgression of Jacob? {Is} it not Samaria? And who {are} the high places of Judah? {Is} it not Jerusalem?
“So I will make Samaria a ruin of the field, a planting place of a vineyard. And I will pour down her stones into the gorge, and her foundations I will uncover.

And all her carved images will be crushed, and all her wages will be burned in the fire, and all her idols I will make a desolation, for from the wages of a prostitute she gathered {them}, and to the wages of a prostitute they will return.”
On account of this I shall lament and wail; I shall go barefoot and naked. I shall make a lamentation like the jackals and mourning like the daughters of an owl.
For her wounds {are} incurable, for it has come to Judah. It has reached to the gate of my people, to Jerusalem.
In Gath, do not declare {it}; weeping, do not weep. In Beth Leaphrah, roll yourself in the dust.
Pass on your way, dweller of Shaphir, {in} nakedness of shame. The dweller of Zaanan has not gone out; the mourning of Beth Ezel will take from you its standing place.
Surely the dweller of Maroth writhes for {something} good, but evil has come down from Yahweh to the gate of Jerusalem.
Harness the chariot to the steeds, dweller of Lachish. She {was} the beginning of sin to daughter Zion, for in you were found the transgressions of Israel.
Therefore you will give dowry gifts to Moresheth Gath. The houses of Achzib {will} become a deception to the kings of Israel.
Also a possessor I will bring to you, dweller of Mareshah. The glory of Israel will come to Adullam.
Make yourself bald and shave for the sons of your delight. Enlarge your baldness like the eagle, for they have gone into exile from you.
Woe to the devisers of iniquity and the workers of evil on their beds! In the light of the morning they do it, for it is in the power of their hand.
And they covet fields and seize {them}, and houses, and take {them} away. And they oppress a man and his house, and a man and his inheritance.
Therefore, thus says Yahweh, “Behold me, devising against this clan disaster, which you will not remove your necks from there, and you will not walk haughtily, for it {is} an evil time.

In that day {someone} will lift up against you a proverb, and lament a lamentation of a lamentation. He says, ‘Destroying, we are destroyed! The portion of my people he exchanges! How he removes {it} from me! To a rebel he divides our fields!’”
Therefore there will not be for you one casting a measuring line by lot in the assembly of Yahweh.
“Do not drip,” they drip. They do not drip about these {things}; disgraces will not depart.
Should it be said, house of Jacob, “Is the Spirit of Yahweh short?” Or “Are these his deeds?” Do not my words do good with the one walking uprightly?
“But recently my people rise up as an enemy. You strip the splendor from the front of the garment, from those passing by in security, {those} returning from war.
The women of my people you drive out from the house of her delights; from upon her infants you take away my splendor forever.
Rise up and go! For this {is} not the resting place; because of uncleanness it will destroy, and a grievous destruction.”
If a man walking {in} wind and falsehood lied, “I will drip to you of wine and of beer,” he would be the dripper of this people.

“Gathering, I will gather Jacob, all of you. Assembling, I will assemble the remnant of Israel. Together I will set them like sheep of Bozrah, like a flock in the midst of its pasture; they will be noisy from humanity.

The breaker has gone up to the face of them. They have broken through and passed through the gate and gone out through it. And their king has passed on to the face of them, and Yahweh {is} at their head.”
And I said, “Hear, please, heads of Jacob and commanders of the house of Israel: Is it not for you to know justice?
Haters of good and lovers of evil, tearing their skin from upon them and their flesh from upon their bones,

and who have eaten the flesh of my people, and their skin from upon them they have stripped, and their bones they have broken, and they have chopped {them} up as {what} is in the pot, and as flesh inside a cauldron.”
Then they will cry out to Yahweh, but he will not answer them. And he will hide his face from them at that time, just as they have made their deeds evil.

Thus says Yahweh, “Concerning the prophets causing my people to wander astray, biting with their teeth, then they call out, ‘Peace!’ But whoever does not put {something} in their mouths, they consecrate war against him.
Therefore, {it will be} night for you without vision, and it will be dark for you without divining. And the sun will go down on the prophets, and the day will become dark over them.”
And the seers will be ashamed, and the diviners will be disgraced. And all of them will cover over the mustache, for there is no answer of God.
But I, in contrast, I am full of power, the Spirit of Yahweh, and justice, and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin.
Hear this, please, heads of the house of Jacob and commanders of the house of Israel, the ones abhorring justice and making all of the straight {things} crooked,
building Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustice.
Her heads judge for a bribe, and her priests teach for a price, and her prophets divine for silver. Yet they lean on Yahweh, saying, “Is not Yahweh in our midst? Evil will not come upon us.”
Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed {as} a field, and Jerusalem will become heaps, and the mountain of the house, as high places of a forest.
But it will be in the last of the days, the mountain of the house of Yahweh will be established as the head of the mountains. And it will be lifted above the hills, and peoples will stream to it.

Many nations will go and say, “Come and let us go up to the mountain of Yahweh, and to the house of the God of Jacob, so that he will teach us from his ways, and so that we may walk in his paths.” For from Zion the law will go out, and the word of Yahweh from Jerusalem.

And he will judge among many peoples and will decide for strong nations far away. And they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, and they will not train for war any more.
And they will sit, each person under his vine and under his fig tree. And there will be no terrorizer, for the mouth of Yahweh of Armies has spoken.
For all the peoples walk, each one, in the name of his god. But we, we will walk in the name of Yahweh our God forever and ever.
“On that day,” declares Yahweh, “I shall assemble the lame and gather the outcast, and those whom I have afflicted.
And I will turn the lame into a remnant, and the ones driven away into a strong nation, and Yahweh will reign over them on Mount Zion, from now and until forever.
And you, watchtower for the flock, hill of daughter Zion— to you it will arrive, and the former dominion will come, the kingdom {belonging} to daughter Jerusalem.
Now, why do you shout a shout? Is there no king among you, or has your counselor perished, that pain grips you like a woman giving birth?

Writhe in pain and burst forth, daughter Zion, like a woman giving birth. For now you will you go out of the city, and live in the field, and go to Babylon. There you will be rescued. There Yahweh will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.

And I shepherded the flock of slaughter, therefore the poor of the flock. And I took for myself two staffs. For the one I called “Favor,” and for the other I called “Union,” and I shepherded the flock.
And I destroyed the three shepherds in one month.
And I said, “I will not shepherd you. The one dying, let it die, and the one being destroyed, let it be destroyed, and the ones remaining, let them eat, each one, the flesh of her companion.”
And I took my staff Favor, and I chopped it up, to break my covenant that I had cut with all the peoples.
And it was broken on that day, and so the poor ones of the flock, the ones watching me, knew that it was the word of Yahweh.
And I said to them, “If it is good in your eyes, give my wages; but if not, refrain.” And they weighed out my wages, thirty {pieces} of silver.

And Yahweh said to me, “Throw it to the potter, the magnificence of the price at which I was valued by them!” And I took the thirty {pieces} of silver and threw it {into} the house of Yahweh, to the potter.
And I chopped up my second staff, Union, to break the brotherhood between Judah and between Israel.
And Yahweh said to me, “Again, take for yourself the equipment of a foolish shepherd,

for behold, I am raising up a shepherd in the land. He will not attend to the ones being destroyed; he will not seek the scattered one; and he will not heal the broken one; he will not sustain the one standing; but he will eat the flesh of the fat one, and he will tear off their hooves.
Woe, worthless shepherd, the one forsaking the flock! A sword against his arm and against his right eye! His arm withering will wither, and his right eye dimming will dim!”
The burden of the word of Yahweh concerning Israel— the declaration of Yahweh, the one stretching out the heavens and founding the earth and forming the spirit of man within him.
“Behold, I am making Jerusalem a cup of staggering for all of the peoples all around. And also against Judah it will be, in the siege against Jerusalem.

On that day”— the declaration of Yahweh— “I will strike every horse with confusion and its rider with madness. But over the house of Judah I will open my eyes, and every horse of the peoples I will strike with blindness.
And the chiefs of Judah will say in their heart, ‘The inhabitants of Jerusalem are a strength to me by Yahweh of Armies, their God.’

On that day I will make the chiefs of Judah like a basin of fire among trees and like a torch of fire in a sheaf, and they will devour on the right and on the left all of the peoples all around. And Jerusalem will dwell again in its place, in Jerusalem.”
And Yahweh will save the tents of Judah at the first, so that the honor of the house of David and the honor of the dweller of Jerusalem will not be great over Judah.

On that day Yahweh will defend on behalf of the inhabitant of Jerusalem, and the stumbler among them on that day will be like David, and the house of David, like God, like the angel of Yahweh to their face.
“And it will be on that day, I will seek to destroy all of the nations coming against Jerusalem.

And I will pour out on the house of David and on the inhabitant of Jerusalem a spirit of favor and supplications, and they will look to me, whom they pierced. And they will mourn over him as the mourning over the only one, and they will be bitter over him as being bitter over the firstborn.”
On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be great, like the mourning of Hadad Rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
And the land will mourn, clans, clans separately: the clan of the house of David separately, and their wives separately; the clan of the house of Nathan separately, and their wives separately,
the clan of the house of Levi separately and their wives separately, the clan of the Shimeite separately and their wives separately,

“And it will happen on that day”—the declaration of Yahweh of Armies—“I will cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they will not be remembered again, and also I will cause the prophets and the spirit of uncleanness to pass from the land.

And it will happen, when a man prophesies again, then his father and his mother, the ones bearing him, will say to him, ‘You will not live, for you have spoken falsehood in the name of Yahweh.’ And his father and his mother, the ones bearing him, will pierce him in his prophesying.
And it will happen on that day, the prophets will have shame, each man from his vision, in his prophesying. And they will not wear a cloak of hair in order to deceive.
And he will say, ‘I am not a prophet. I am a man working the ground, for a man has owned me from my youth.’
And {someone} will say to him, ‘What are these wounds between your hands?’ And he will say, ‘Those are the ones with which I was struck {in} the house of my lovers.’

“And I will gather all the nations to Jerusalem for the battle, and the city will be captured, and the houses will be plundered, and the women will be raped. And half of the city will go out into the exile, but the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.”
And Yahweh will go out and will fight against those nations, like the day of his fighting on a day of battle.

And it will be one day— it, it will be known to Yahweh— not day and not night. And it will happen, at the time of evening there will be light.
And it will happen on that day, living waters will go out from Jerusalem, half of them to the eastern sea and half of them to the western sea; it will happen in the summer and in the winter.

And it will happen on that day, a great tumult of Yahweh will be among them, and each man will seize the hand of his neighbor, and his hand will go up against the hand of his neighbor.

And thus will be the plague of the horse, the mule, the camel, and the donkey, and every beast that will be in those camps, like this plague.

And it will happen, everyone remaining from all the nations, the ones coming against Jerusalem, will go up as often as year by year to bow down to the King, Yahweh of Armies, and to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
And it will happen, whoever does not go up from the clans of the earth to Jerusalem to bow down to the King, Yahweh of Armies— on them there will not be the rain.
And if the clan of Egypt does not go up and does not come, then not on them. There will be the plague with which Yahweh strikes the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
This will be the sin of Egypt and the sin of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
On that day there will be on the bells of the horse, “Holy to Yahweh.” And the pots in the house of Yahweh will be like the bowls to the face of the altar.

And every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah will be holy to Yahweh of Armies, and all the ones sacrificing will come and will take from them and will boil in them. And there will not be a Canaanite again in the house of Yahweh of Armies on that day.
The burden of the word of Yahweh to Israel by the hand of Malachi.
“I have loved you,” says Yahweh. But you say, “In what have you loved us?” “{Was} not Esau a brother to Jacob?” the declaration of Yahweh. “Yet I loved Jacob,
but Esau I hated. And I made his mountains a desolation and his inheritance for the jackals of the wilderness.”

Though Edom says, “We are beaten down, but we will return and build the ruins,” thus says Yahweh of Armies: “They themselves may build, but I myself will tear down. And they will call them ‘the territory of wickedness’ and ‘the people whom Yahweh abhors forever.’
And your eyes will see, and you yourselves will say, ‘Great is Yahweh beyond the border of Israel!’

A son honors a father, and a servant his master. So if I am a father, where is my honor? And if I am a master, where is my fear?” says Yahweh of Armies to you, O priests, despisers of my name. But you say, “In what have we despised your name?”
“{You are} presenting defiled food upon my altar. But you say, ‘In what have we defiled you?’ In your saying, ‘The table of Yahweh, it is despised.’

And when you present the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? And when you present the lame and the sick, is it not evil? Present it now to your governor. Will he accept you or lift up your face?” says Yahweh of Armies.
“And now, please entreat the face of God, that he may be gracious to us. This has been from your hand. Will he lift up your faces?” says Yahweh of Armies.

“But cursed {be} the deceiver if a male is in his flock and he vows {it}, but he sacrifices the blemished to the Lord. For I {am} a great King, says Yahweh of Armies, and my name is feared among the nations.

“So I myself have also made you despised and humiliated before all the people, because you {are} not keeping my ways and {are} lifting faces regarding the instruction.”
{Is} not one father to all of us? Did not one God create us? Why do we deal treacherously, a man against his brother, to profane the covenant of our fathers?

Judah has dealt treacherously, and an abomination has been done in Israel and in Jerusalem. For Judah has profaned the holy place of Yahweh, which he loves, and has married the daughter of a foreign god.
May Yahweh cut off from the tents of Jacob the man who does this, the one being awake and the one answering, even the one bringing an offering to Yahweh of Armies.

And I will draw near to you for judgment. And I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, and against the adulterers, and against the ones swearing to a lie, and against the ones oppressing the wage of the hired worker, the widow, and the orphan, and the ones turning aside the foreigner, and they do not fear me,” says Yahweh of Armies.

Bring all of the tithe to the house of treasure, and let there be food in my house. And test me now in this,” says Yahweh of Armies, “if I will not open for you the windows of the heavens and pour out for you a blessing until there is no sufficiency.

“And all of the nations will bless you, for you will be a land of delight,” says Yahweh of Armies.
“Your words have been strong against me,” says Yahweh. “But you say, ‘What have we spoken {among ourselves} against you?’
You have said, ‘Serving God {is} worthless. And what profit, that we have kept his charge and that we have walked mournfully to the face of Yahweh of Armies?

Then the ones fearing Yahweh spoke {among themselves}, a man with his neighbor. And Yahweh paid attention and heard. And a book of remembrance was written to his face for the ones fearing Yahweh and for the ones esteeming his name.

“And they will be to me,” says Yahweh of Armies, “a special possession on the day that I {am} preparing. And I will have compassion on them just as a man has compassion on his son, the one serving him.
And you will return and see between the righteous and to the wicked, between the one serving God and to {one} who does not serve him.

But for you fearers of my name, the sun of righteousness will rise, and healing {will be} upon its wings. And you will go out and skip like calves of the stall.

“Remember the instruction of Moses my servant, which I commanded him at Horeb for all of Israel, the statutes and the judgments.
Behold, I {am} sending to you Elijah the prophet to the face of the coming of the great and fearsome day of Yahweh.
And he will turn the heart of the fathers to the sons, and the heart of the sons to their fathers, lest I come and strike the land {with} a curse.”
The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham:

and Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar, and Perez fathered Hezrom, and Hezrom fathered Aram,
and Aram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon,
and Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab, and Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth, and Obed fathered Jesse,
and Jesse fathered David the king, and David fathered Solomon by the {wife} of Uriah,
and Solomon fathered Rehoboam, and Rehoboam fathered Abijah, and Abijah fathered Asaph,
and Asaph fathered Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Ozias,

and Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, and Manasseh fathered Amos, and Amos fathered Josiah,
and Josiah fathered Jechoniah and his brothers at the Babylonian deportation,
and after the Babylonian deportation, Jechoniah fathered Salathiel, and Salathiel fathered Zerubbabel,
and Zerubbabel fathered Abiud, and Abiud fathered Eliakim, and Eliakim fathered Azor,
and Azor fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Achim, and Achim fathered Eliud,

Therefore, all the generations from Abraham until David {were} 14 generations, and from David until the Babylonian deportation {were} 14 generations, and from the Babylonian deportation until the Christ {were} 14 generations.
Now the birth of Jesus Christ was thus: His mother, Mary, having been engaged to marry Joseph, before they came together, was found having in the womb from the Holy Spirit.
Now Joseph her husband, being righteous, and not wanting to publicly disgrace her, intended to divorce her secretly.

But he having reflected on these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him by way of a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, you should not fear to take Mary as your wife, because the one having been conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
And she will bear a son, and you will call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.”
Now all this happened so that might be fulfilled {what} was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying,
“Behold, the virgin will have in her womb and bear a son, and they will call his name Immanuel”—which is translated, “God with us.”
And Joseph, having been awakened from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord commanded him and took her {as} his wife.
And he did not know her until she bore a son. And he called his name Jesus.
Now, Jesus having been born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, learned men from the east arrived in Jerusalem,
saying, “Where is the one having been born King of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east and came to worship him.”
But having heard this, Herod the king became troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
And having brought together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired from them, “Where is the Christ being born?”
And they said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for thus it has been written through the prophet,

Then Herod, having secretly called the learned men, inquired from them the time of the appearing of the star.
And having sent them to Bethlehem, he said, “Having gone, search carefully for the young child, and after you have found him, report to me so that I also, having come, might worship him.”
And they, having heard the king, went, and behold, the star that they saw in the east was going before them until, having come, it stood over where the young child was.

Blessed {are} the pure in heart, for they will see God.
Blessed {are} the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God.
Blessed {are} the ones persecuted for the sake of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.
Blessed are you when they insult you and persecute {you} and say every evil thing against you, lying, because of me.
Rejoice and be very glad, for your reward {is} great in the heavens, for in this way they persecuted the prophets before you.
You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt is made tasteless, with what might it be made salty again? It is good for nothing any longer, except having been thrown out, to be trampled by men.
You are the light of the world. A city being set on top of a mountain is not able to be hidden.
Neither do they light a lamp and put it under a basket, but rather on the lampstand, and it shines for all the ones in the house.
Let your light shine before men in such a way so that they might see your good deeds and might glorify your Father in the heavens.
Do not think that I came to destroy the law or the prophets. I came not to destroy but to fulfill.
For truly I say to you, until the heaven and the earth passes away, one jot or one tittle will certainly not pass away from the law until all things are accomplished.

Therefore, whoever annuls one of the least of these commandments and teaches men to do so will be called least in the kingdom of the heavens. But whoever does and teaches {them}, that one will be called great in the kingdom of the heavens.
For I say to you that unless your righteousness abounds more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will certainly not enter into the kingdom of the heavens.
You have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘Do not kill,’ and, ‘Whoever kills will be subject to the judgment.’

But I say to you that everyone being angry with his brother will be subject to the judgment. And whoever says to his brother, ‘Raka!’ will be subject to the council. And whoever says, ‘You fool!’ will be subject to the Gehenna of fire.
Therefore, if you offer your gift at the altar and there you remember that your brother has something against you,
leave your gift there in front of the altar and go; first be reconciled with your brother, and then, having come, offer your gift.
Be in agreement with your accuser quickly while you are with him on the way, lest your accuser might hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you will be thrown into prison.
Truly I say to you, you will certainly not come out from there until you have paid the last quadrans.
You have heard that it was said, ‘Do not commit adultery.’
But I say to you that everyone looking at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

But if your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw {it} away from you. For it is better for you that one of your members would perish and your whole body would not be thrown into Gehenna.
And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw {it} away from you. For it is better for you that one of your members would perish and your whole body would not go into Gehenna.
Now it has been said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce.’
But I say to you that everyone divorcing his wife, except for a report of sexual immorality, causes her to commit adultery. And whoever marries {the one who} has been divorced commits adultery.
Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘Do not break an oath, but carry out your oaths to the Lord.’
But I tell you not to swear at all, neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God;
nor by the earth, for it is a footstool for his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
Neither should you swear by your head, for you are not able to make one hair white or black.
But let your word be ‘Yes, yes,’ {or} ‘No, no.’ But anything greater than this is from the evil one.
You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye in exchange for an eye, and a tooth in exchange for a tooth.’
But I tell you not to resist the evil one. Instead, whoever strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.
And to the one wanting to have judgment passed upon you and to take away your tunic, let him also have your cloak.
And whoever will press you into service for one mile, go with him two.
Give to the one asking you, and do not turn away from the one wanting to borrow from you.
You have heard that it was said, ‘Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
But I say to you, love your enemies and pray on behalf of the ones persecuting you
so that you might be sons of your Father in the heavens. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and he sends rain on the just and the unjust.
For if you love the ones loving you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same thing?
And if you greet only your brothers, what do you do more? Do not even the Gentiles do the same thing?
Therefore, you shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
Now take heed not to do your righteousness before men to be seen by them, otherwise, you do not have a reward with your Father in the heavens.

So when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before yourself even as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets so that they may be glorified by men. Truly I say to you, they have their reward in full.
But you, giving alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing
so that your alms may be in secret, and your Father seeing in secret will reward you.

And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, for they love to pray, having stood in the synagogues and on the corners of the street, so that they may be seen by men. Truly I say to you, they have their reward in full.
But you, when you pray, enter into your inner chamber, and having shut your door, pray to your Father in secret, and your Father seeing in secret will reward you.
Now praying, do not make useless repetitions even as the Gentiles, for they think that because of their many words they will be heard.
Therefore, you should not be like them, for your Father knows what need you have before you ask him.
Therefore, you must pray like this: ‘Our Father in the heavens, let your name be made holy.
Let your kingdom come, let your will be done as in heaven also on earth.
Give us today our daily bread;
and forgive us our debts, as we also forgave our debtors;

For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
But if you do not forgive the men, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

But you, {when} fasting, anoint your head and wash your face
so that you would not be seen as fasting by men, but only by your Father in secret; and your Father, seeing in secret, will reward you.
Do not store up for yourselves treasures on the earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.
Instead, store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves do not break in nor steal.
For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
The lamp of the body is the eye. Therefore, if your eye is healthy, your whole body will be illuminated.
But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be dark. Therefore, if the light in you is darkness, how great {is} the darkness!
No one is able to serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and will love the other, or else he will be devoted to one and will despise the other. You are not able to serve God and wealth.

Because of this I say to you, do not worry about your life, what you might eat or what you might drink, nor about your body, what you might wear. Is not life more than food, and the body, {than} clothing?
Look at the birds of the sky, that they do not sow nor reap nor gather into barns, but your heavenly Father feeds them. {Are} you not more valuable than they?
But which of you, being anxious, is able to add one cubit to his lifespan?
And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field—how they grow. They do not labor, neither do they spin.
But I say to you that not even Solomon in all his glory clothed himself like one of these.
But if God thus clothes the grass of the field, existing today and tomorrow being thrown into an oven, {will he} not much more you, ones of little faith?
Therefore, you should not be anxious, saying, ‘What might we eat?’ or, ‘What might we drink?’ or, ‘What might we wear?’
For the Gentiles seek all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all of these things.
But seek first the kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.
Therefore, you should not be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day {is} its evil.
Do not judge, so that you will not be judged.
For with the judgment by which you judge, you will be judged, and with the measure by which you measure, it will be measured to you.
Now why do you look at the speck of wood that {is} in the eye of your brother, but you do not notice the log in your eye?
Or how will you say to your brother, ‘Let me take out the speck of wood from your eye,’ while behold, the log {is} in your eye?
You hypocrite! First take out the log from your eye, and then you will see clearly to take out the speck of wood from the eye of your brother.

You should neither give the holy to the dogs nor should you throw your pearls in front of the pigs. Otherwise, they will trample them under their feet, and having turned, they will tear you to pieces.
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone asking receives; and the one seeking finds; and to the one knocking, it will be opened.
Or what man is there from among you, of whom his son will ask for bread—he will not give him a stone, will he?
Or he will also ask for a fish—he will not give him a snake, will he?
Therefore, if you, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in the heavens give good things to the ones asking him?
Therefore, all things in as much as you desire that men do to you, in this manner also, you do to them, for this is the Law and the Prophets.
Enter through the narrow gate. For wide {is} the gate and broad {is} the road that is leading to destruction, and there are many entering through it.
For the gate {is} narrow and the road has been made narrow that is leading to life, and there are few finding it.

By their fruits you will recognize them. They do not gather grapes from a thornbush or figs from thistles, do they?
In the same way, every good tree produces good fruits, but the rotten tree produces bad fruits.
A good tree is not able to produce bad fruits, nor a rotten tree to produce good fruits.
Every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into a fire.
So then, by their fruits you will recognize them.
Not everyone saying to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into the kingdom of the heavens, but the one doing the will of my Father in the heavens.
Many will say to me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and in your name cast out demons, and in your name do many mighty deeds?’
And then I will publicly declare to them, ‘I never knew you! Go away from me, the ones practicing lawlessness!’
Therefore, everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be compared to a wise man who built his house upon the rock.
And the rain came down, and the floods came, and the winds blew and struck against that house, but it did not fall down, for it had been founded on the rock.
But everyone hearing these words of mine and not doing them will be compared to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand.
And the rain came down, and the floods came, and the winds blew and struck against that house, and it fell, and its destruction was great.”

And he says to them, “Why are you cowardly, you of little faith?” Then, having gotten up, he rebuked the winds and the sea, and a great calm happened.
But the men marveled, saying, “What sort of {man} is he, that even the winds and the sea obey him?”

And {when} he had come to the other side, to the region of the Gadarenes, two men met him, being possessed by demons, coming out of the tombs, very violent, so that no one was strong enough to pass through that road.
